   the IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) V8.5.6.0 cumulative fix
   1, the server does not start and SQLCODE=-952 database errors
   like the following errors are logged in the
   <profile_root>/logs/BPMUpdateSystemApp*.log file:

 *  If you have many entries in the LSW_PO_VERSIONS table of the IBM
    Process Server database, a value that is too small for the Java
    maximum heap size is set when the BPMUpdateSystemApp admin
   command runs to update the IBM BPM toolkits and process
   applications.
- `E5.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION

- `E2.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  When you place your inbound web service  inside a toolkit and
   one parameter is defined as a complex type list, the inbound
   web service generated WSDL contains an array type definition
   in a non-existent namespace and the runtime-generated SOAP
   message does not accomplish the WSDL definition. As a result,
   the web service client reports an error when loading the wrong
   WSDL or parsing the SOAP response message.

- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  IBM Business Process Manager (BPM)          *
   *                  Advanced                                    *
   *                  IBM BPM Express                             *
   *                  IBM BPM Standard                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When you place your inbound web         *
   *                      service  inside a toolkit and one       *
   *                      parameter is defined as a complex       *
   *                      type list, the inbound web service      *
   *                      generated WSDL contains an array type   *
   *                      definition in a non-existent            *
   *                      namespace and the runtime-generated     *
   *                      SOAP message does not accomplish the    *
   *                      WSDL definition. As a result, the web   *
   *                      service client reports an error when    *
   *                      loading the wrong WSDL or parsing the   *
   *                      SOAP response message.                  *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   When you put the inbound web service inside a toolkit, the
   WSDL might use the namespace of the toolkit instead of the
   process application namespace. As a result, the array list
   items are created with the wrong namespace and wrong WSDL and
   a wrong SOAP message are generated.
- `E2.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  A fix is available for IBM BPM V8.5.5.0 that ensures the
   correct namespace is used no matter where the web service is
   placed.

## techqa_DEV_Q300#row-0109

Question:
DB2 Non Reclaimable Storage . We have tablespaces defined under DB2 9.5 that apparently are not able
to reclaim storage back to the OS, but does that mean DB2 cannot reuse
this space as well?


Reference / gold answer:
No, DB2 not being able to reclaim storage back to the OS does not mean that it cannot reuse the space. DB2 has mechanisms in place, such as the Buddy Space mechanism, to manage and reuse storage space efficiently within tablespaces. The space that cannot be reclaimed may still be available for reuse within the database for storing new data.

Reference evidence:
- `1b`:  Receiving SQL1763N error with Reason Code 11 while running "Alter Tablespace" command to reclaim unused storage space against DMS or automatic storage tablespaces. SYMPTOM
- `1j`: MON_GET_TABLESPACE table function and RECLAIMABLE_SPACE_ENABLED monitor element can be used to identify whether the tablespace is enabled for reclaimable storage or not. Example:
- `1s`: Otherwise, it returns a value of 0.
- `1t`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `1u`: To use the reclaimable storage feature, make sure to create the DMS or automatic storage tablespaces in DB2 Version 9.7 or later.
- `1v`: Example testcase on SYSCATSPACE DMS tablespace which has reclaimable storage enabled.  *  *  *  *  * Note:

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  If the root of the automatic storage path does not have enough
   free file system space, and an attempt is made to extend the
   tablespace, DB2 will incorrectly report SQL0968C "file system
   full" without checking the amount of free file system space
   in the full path where the new container should be created.
   .
   For example, say that the following automatic storage path
   is defined (output taken from a database snapshot):
   .
   Automatic storage path                     = /home/db2inst1
   .
   An attempt is made to extend the tablespace. A new container
   is about to be created in the following path consisting of
   the automatic storage path, instance name, node number,
   database name, and tablespace id:
   .
   /home/db2inst1/db2inst1/NODE0000/SAMPLE/T0000004/
   .
   However, DB2 will not check the amount of free disk space
   in this long path where the container is going to be created.
   Instead, only "/home/db2inst1" is considered. This is an
   incorrect assumption since "/home/db2inst1" can contain
   mounted filesystems, for example "/home/db2inst1/db2inst1",
   which can have a sufficient amount of free disk space.
   .
   DB2 should always check the target path where the new
   container is going to be created, not just the root of it.
   If the target path does not exist, DB2 will check the file
   system information of the last subdirectory in the existing
   path. For example, if only
   .
   /home/db2inst1/db2inst1/NODE0000/
   .
   exists, DB2 will check the amount of free space in this
   directory.
- `E4.S5`: LOCAL FIX
 *  Ensure the root of the automatic storage path has a sufficient
   amount of free file system space.

- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E5.S2`: QUESTION
 How does DB2 perform LOB Space Allocation and Management
- `E5.S3`: ANSWER
DB2 stores most row data in fixed size (4KB, 8KB, 16KB, 32KB) pages. This data is referenced by queries via bufferpool access, i.e. it is read from disk into bufferpool memory to be worked on.
LOB (large object) data is handled differently. A LOB (CLOB - character large object, BLOB – binary large object, or DBCLOB - double byte large object) is stored outside regular row based storage. A LOB can be up to 2GB in size (1GB for a logged LOB). The necessity of handling large amounts of data of potentially very disparate sizes efficiently is what drives the LOB storage mechanism.
- `E5.S4`: There is a descriptor in the regular row data that points to the actual LOB data itself. The size of this descriptor varies from 60 to 312 bytes, depending on the size defined for the LOB in the definition of the table. The actual size of the LOB data is also included in the descriptor. If a row's LOB is defined with an inline size, then, if the entire LOB will fit, it will be inlined into the regular data page. If the LOB data is larger than the inline size, none of the LOB will be inlined. If the actual LOB size is smaller than the descriptor size, it will be implicitly inlined, even if no inlining is defined in the table definition.
- `E5.S5`: All LOB data that does not get inlined as described above will be stored as follows.
- `E5.S6`: LOB data has two components, LBA and LB. The LBA object contains all space allocation information. The LB object contains the actual LOB data. If the tablespace is defined as using System Managed Storage (SMS), then these two objects can be seen as separate files, with .LBA and .LB file extensions. Data in the LBA object passes through the bufferpool. Data in the LB object is not buffered by DB2. Some memory buffering of LB data can be obtained by utilizing the OS file system cache.
- `E5.S7`: The LOB space storage uses what is called a Buddy Space mechanism. There are two types of buddy space - Super Buddy Space (SBS) and Regular Buddy Space (RBS). SBSes control allocation of large segments of data, from 256k to 64m bytes. An RBS controls allocation of segments of size 1k (the minimum LOB allocation unit) to 128KB. There are multiple RBSes per SBS.
- `E5.S8`: In an empty table, there is just one SBS. We then insert a 50KB LOB. As the LOB is inserted, the SBS gets subdivided (always by a factor of 2) until, eventually, we have an RBS segment of a size that can completely contain the LOB, i.e. the RBS size will be 64K. Since we always subdivide by factors of 2, at this stage we will have the occupied segment, and a free buddy segment of 64k, as well as free buddy segments back up the chain at the 128KB (RBS), 256KB(SBS), 512KB(SBS) size, and so on.

- `E1.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM

- `E3.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  If the root of the automatic storage path does not have enough
   free file system space, and an attempt is made to extend the
   tablespace, DB2 will incorrectly report SQL0968C "file system
   full" without checking the amount of free file system space
   in the full path where the new container should be created.
   .
   For example, say that the following automatic storage path
   is defined (output taken from a database snapshot):
   .
   Automatic storage path                     = /home/db2inst1
   .
   An attempt is made to extend the tablespace. A new container
   is about to be created in the following path consisting of
   the automatic storage path, instance name, node number,
   database name, and tablespace id:
   .
   /home/db2inst1/db2inst1/NODE0000/SAMPLE/T0000004/
   .
   However, DB2 will not check the amount of free disk space
   in this long path where the container is going to be created.
   Instead, only "/home/db2inst1" is considered. This is an
   incorrect assumption since "/home/db2inst1" can contain
   mounted filesystems, for example "/home/db2inst1/db2inst1",
   which can have a sufficient amount of free disk space.
   .
   DB2 should always check the target path where the new
   container is going to be created, not just the root of it.
   If the target path does not exist, DB2 will check the file
   system information of the last subdirectory in the existing
   path. For example, if only
   .
   /home/db2inst1/db2inst1/NODE0000/
   .
   exists, DB2 will check the amount of free space in this
   directory.
- `E3.S5`: LOCAL FIX
 *  Ensure the root of the automatic storage path has a sufficient
   amount of free file system space.

- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E5.S2`: QUESTION
 How does DB2 perform LOB Space Allocation and Management
- `E5.S3`: ANSWER
DB2 stores most row data in fixed size (4KB, 8KB, 16KB, 32KB) pages. This data is referenced by queries via bufferpool access, i.e. it is read from disk into bufferpool memory to be worked on.
LOB (large object) data is handled differently. A LOB (CLOB - character large object, BLOB – binary large object, or DBCLOB - double byte large object) is stored outside regular row based storage. A LOB can be up to 2GB in size (1GB for a logged LOB). The necessity of handling large amounts of data of potentially very disparate sizes efficiently is what drives the LOB storage mechanism.
- `E5.S4`: There is a descriptor in the regular row data that points to the actual LOB data itself. The size of this descriptor varies from 60 to 312 bytes, depending on the size defined for the LOB in the definition of the table. The actual size of the LOB data is also included in the descriptor. If a row's LOB is defined with an inline size, then, if the entire LOB will fit, it will be inlined into the regular data page. If the LOB data is larger than the inline size, none of the LOB will be inlined. If the actual LOB size is smaller than the descriptor size, it will be implicitly inlined, even if no inlining is defined in the table definition.
- `E5.S5`: All LOB data that does not get inlined as described above will be stored as follows.
- `E5.S6`: LOB data has two components, LBA and LB. The LBA object contains all space allocation information. The LB object contains the actual LOB data. If the tablespace is defined as using System Managed Storage (SMS), then these two objects can be seen as separate files, with .LBA and .LB file extensions. Data in the LBA object passes through the bufferpool. Data in the LB object is not buffered by DB2. Some memory buffering of LB data can be obtained by utilizing the OS file system cache.
- `E5.S7`: The LOB space storage uses what is called a Buddy Space mechanism. There are two types of buddy space - Super Buddy Space (SBS) and Regular Buddy Space (RBS). SBSes control allocation of large segments of data, from 256k to 64m bytes. An RBS controls allocation of segments of size 1k (the minimum LOB allocation unit) to 128KB. There are multiple RBSes per SBS.
- `E5.S8`: In an empty table, there is just one SBS. We then insert a 50KB LOB. As the LOB is inserted, the SBS gets subdivided (always by a factor of 2) until, eventually, we have an RBS segment of a size that can completely contain the LOB, i.e. the RBS size will be 64K. Since we always subdivide by factors of 2, at this stage we will have the occupied segment, and a free buddy segment of 64k, as well as free buddy segments back up the chain at the 128KB (RBS), 256KB(SBS), 512KB(SBS) size, and so on.

## techqa_DEV_Q047#row-0156

Question:
I need to move my perpetual license of SPSS v24 to my new machine. I have my authorization code first given to me, but since we did not renew our support contract we can't seem to download the software. I was originally told that I could download the trial version and it would have the authorization wizard where I could input the code and move forward. But the only downloadable version is subscription version with no authorization wizard. How do I move forward? 

Reference / gold answer:
Since you are unable to download the software due to an expired Subscription and Maintenance, you have a few options to move your perpetual license of SPSS v24 to your new machine:

1. Contact IBM Sales Department: Reach out to your local IBM Sales Department through their website [https://www.ibm.com/planetwide/] and inquire about obtaining a Media CD copy of the software version corresponding to your perpetual license. This will allow you to install the software on your new machine using the provided authorization code.

2. Contact IBM SPSS Customer Support: If you are unable to download the software or obtain a Media CD copy, contact IBM SPSS Customer Support [http://www.ibm.com/planetwide/region.html] for assistance in transferring your perpetual license to your new machine without the need for a download.

3. Check for alternative methods: If none of the above options work, consider exploring alternative methods provided by IBM SPSS Customer Support to help you move your perpetual license to your new machine despite the limitations imposed by the expired Subscription and Maintenance.

Reference evidence:
- `0d`: The method for acquiring the lock code for a product installation varies by the product and operating system.
- `4a`: entitlements; software; download TECHNOTE (FAQ) QUESTION
- `4b`:  Can I download the software without active Subscription and Maintenance? CAUSE expired entitlements ANSWER
- `4c`: Official statement by IBM eCustomer Care Team (Passport Advantage Online help desk):
- `4d`: We would like to inform you that you can only access and download software that has active Subscription and Maintenance from Passport Advantage Online.
- `4e`: If the Software Subscription and Maintenance has expired you will not be able to download the software from Passport Advantage Online.
- `4f`: In this case, you would need to renew your software Subscription and Maintenance.
- `4g`: You can order the Media CD copy of the software your company purchased.
- `4h`: The software version is the one up to the time your subscription has expired.
- `4i`: The sales department will be able to advise you if the Media CD is available.
- `4j`: You can find your local contact for the IBM Sales Department at: https://www.ibm.com/planetwide/ [https://www.ibm.com/planetwide/]

=== CANDIDATE A ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: product key authorization license TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 I am attempting to license the SPSS Sentinel License Manager for my SPSS products. Entering the authorization code/license code produces an error:
- `E1.S3`: Sentinel LM: Error[19]: Failed to add license code to the license server on host "". License code is invalid.
- `E1.S4`: followed by...
- `E1.S5`: Error Code: 30019
- `E1.S6`: The License Code that you entered is not valid. Please enter a License Code from SPSS. Possibly you entered the Authorization Code that came with your product. If you did, click Back and use your Authorization Code to get a license from SPSS via the Internet, Telephone, or E-mail.
- `E1.S7`: Lock Code:
Authorization Code:
License Code:
- `E1.S8`: What is the problem?
- `E1.S9`: ANSWER
1. The Lock Code encrypted into the entered license does not match that of the hardware you are attempting to license. If you are unable to determine which server for which this license was generated, please contact IBM SPSS Customer Support [http://www.ibm.com/planetwide/region.html].
- `E1.S10`: 2. You are attempting to license your installation via a Terminal Services/Citrix session with a single or site authorization/license. If you intend to run the software via Terminal Services/Citrix, you will need to obtain a Network license. Please contact your local IBM Sales office [http://www.ibm.com/planetwide/region.html]. If you intend to run the application on a server-class machine without Terminal Services/Citrix or you are licensing a server based product, e.g. SPSS Server, please go to that machine directly and run the License Authorization Wizard to request/submit a license.
- `E1.S11`: 3. You are entering a network authorization code into the License Authorization Wizard installed with SPSS for Windows, SPSS Text Analysis for Surveys, or AMOS. The network authorization code is required to license the SPSS Sentinel License Manager, not the aforementioned applications. At this point, you must contact IBM SPSS Customer Support [http://www.ibm.com/planetwide/region.html] and request a new authorization as the network authorization code is only valid for one machine. Once you receive the new authorization code, please launch the License Authorization Wizard installed with the SPSS Sentinel License Manager (Start->Programs->SPSS Sentinel License Manager->SPSS License Authorization Wizard) and enter your authorization code when prompted.
- `E1.S12`: 4. Ensure the SPSS Sentinel License Manager service is started. Go to Start->Control Panel->Administrative Tools->Services and locate "Sentinel LM". The status should report the service is started. If it is not started, i.e. blank, right-click/double-click on the "Sentinel LM" service name and select "Start". If the service will not start, one possible cause could be the Sentinel License Manager was previously installed elsewhere, but has since been removed and installed into a different directory. If that is the case, go to Start->Programs->SPSS Sentinel License Manager->Service Loader. Next, ensure the "Executable Path" is correct and click "Add". Finally, start the "Sentinel LM" service following the aforementioned steps.
- `E1.S13`: 5. You have an lshost or lsforcehost environment variable defined on the machine where the SPSS Sentinel License Manager is installed. Please remove the environment variable and run the License Authorization Wizard again on this machine to request a license.
- `E1.S14`: 6. You are not logged in as 'root' while attempting to license the SPSS Sentinel License Manager on a non-Windows platform.
- `E1.S15`: 5. You have an lshost or lsforcehost environment variable defined on the machine where the SPSS Sentinel License Manager is installed. Please remove the environment variable and run the License Authorization Wizard again on this machine to request a license.

- `E2.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 I am an IT administrator for an organization. My IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0 client licenses are expiring. I have purchased IBM SPSS Statistics 24.0 client software and licenses, but I am afraid my version 23.0 licenses will expire before I complete my client migrations to Statistics 24.0. How can I keep my end users up and running throughout the migration?
- `E2.S3`: CAUSE
License for version N expires before all clients can be upgraded to client software version N+1
- `E2.S4`: ANSWER
Starting in IBM SPSS Statistics 22.0 we have added what we colloquially call "N+1 Licensing" for this exact problem. Simply put, your Statistics version "N" will use client licenses for Statistics version "N+1".
- `E2.S5`: Imagine the above scenario. You have IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0 clients deployed and the license period is coming to an end. Your licenses for Statistics 23.0 will expire long before you complete the upgrade of all clients to Statistics 24.0. The solution is to go ahead and deploy your Statistics 24.0 licenses. Statistics 23.0 (version "N") will use a Statistics 24.0 (version "N+1") license.
- `E2.S6`: This is true for Authorized User licensing.
- `E2.S7`: This is true for Concurrent User licensing - though as a solution, it really is more suited to this method.
- `E2.S8`: CAVEATS:
- `E2.S9`: 1) If you are deploying multiple license strings (e.g. A 'base' license plus one or more add-on licenses) the 'base' and 'add-on' license versions must match.
- `E2.S10`: For example: You have IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0 client installed.
- `E2.S11`: You CAN add a version 23.0 IBM SPSS Statistics Advanced Statistics module to your version 23.0 "IBM SPSS Statistics Base" installation
You CANNOT add a version 24.0 IBM SPSS Statistics Advanced Statistics module to your version 23.0 "IBM SPSS Statistics Base" installation license.
- `E2.S12`: You CAN add a version 24.0 IBM SPSS Statistics Advanced Statistics module to your version 24.0 "IBM SPSS Statistics Base" installation license.
- `E2.S13`: 2) "N+1 Licensing" will not work with Commuter License tokens. IBM SPSS Statistics version "N" can use an IBM SPSS Statistics "N+1" Concurrent User license token. However, it cannot use the same as a Commuter license token.
- `E2.S14`: RELATED INFORMATION

Need more help? Our Licensing forum is Live! [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/topics/spsslicensing.html]

- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 Can I download the software without active Subscription and Maintenance?
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
expired entitlements
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
- `E3.S5`: Official statement by IBM eCustomer Care Team (Passport Advantage Online help desk):
- `E3.S6`: We would like to inform you that you can only access and download software that has active Subscription and Maintenance from Passport Advantage Online.
If the Software Subscription and Maintenance has expired you will not be able to download the software from Passport Advantage Online.
In this case, you would need to renew your software Subscription and Maintenance.
- `E3.S7`: You can order the Media CD copy of the software your company purchased. The software version is the one up to the time your subscription has expired.
The sales department will be able to advise you if the Media CD is available.

- `E4.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 I have been requested to provide the 'lock code' for my SPSS product and/or License Manager. How do I determine the lock code for my SPSS product/License Manager?
- `E4.S3`: ANSWER
The method for acquiring the lock code for a product installation varies by the product and operating system.
Desktop/Client Product Installations
- `E4.S4`: Windows operating systems
(1) Select Start.
(2) Select 'Programs' (or 'All Programs') menu entry.
(3) Select the program folder corresponding to the product (example: 'IBM SPSS Statistics')
(4) Launch the 'License Authorization' program corresponding to the product version (example: 'IBM SPSS Statistics 24 License Authorization Wizard')
(5) Select the 'Next' button.
(6) In the lower left section of this window will appear 'Lock Code for this machine is'. Note the indicated lock code.
(7) Select the 'Cancel button'.
(8) Select the 'Yes' button. The License Authorization program will close.
- `E4.S5`: MacOS operating systems
(1) Open Finder.
(2) Select 'Go' menu.
(3) Select 'Applications' entry.
(4) Select 'IBM' icon.
(5) Select 'SPSS' folder icon.
(6) Select folder icon corresponding to the product (example: 'Statistics')
(7) Select the folder corresponding to the product version (example: '24').
(8) Launch 'License Authorization Wizard' program.
(9) Select the 'License my product now' option.
(10) Select 'Next'.
(11) In the lower left section of this window will appear 'Lock Code for this machine is'. Note the indicated lock code.
(12) Select the 'Cancel button'.
(13) Select the 'Yes' button. The License Authorization program will close.
- `E4.S6`: License Manager
- `E4.S7`: License Manager on Windows Operating Systems
(1a) Open an Administrator Command Prompt. 
(1b) The Command Prompt title bar must read 'Administrator: Command Prompt' or the procedure may not execute properly.
(2a) Change directory ('cd') to the License Manager installation directory. 
(2b) If unsure as to the location of the License Manager installation directory, see TechNote 1989514 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21989514].
(3) Execute the following command: echoid
(4) The response will include a value associated with 'Locking code 1'.
(5) This is the License Manager lock code.
- `E4.S8`: License Manager on Linux [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21484024]

- `E1.S10`: 2. You are attempting to license your installation via a Terminal Services/Citrix session with a single or site authorization/license. If you intend to run the software via Terminal Services/Citrix, you will need to obtain a Network license. Please contact your local IBM Sales office [http://www.ibm.com/planetwide/region.html]. If you intend to run the application on a server-class machine without Terminal Services/Citrix or you are licensing a server based product, e.g. SPSS Server, please go to that machine directly and run the License Authorization Wizard to request/submit a license.
- `E1.S11`: 3. You are entering a network authorization code into the License Authorization Wizard installed with SPSS for Windows, SPSS Text Analysis for Surveys, or AMOS. The network authorization code is required to license the SPSS Sentinel License Manager, not the aforementioned applications. At this point, you must contact IBM SPSS Customer Support [http://www.ibm.com/planetwide/region.html] and request a new authorization as the network authorization code is only valid for one machine. Once you receive the new authorization code, please launch the License Authorization Wizard installed with the SPSS Sentinel License Manager (Start->Programs->SPSS Sentinel License Manager->SPSS License Authorization Wizard) and enter your authorization code when prompted.
- `E1.S12`: 4. Ensure the SPSS Sentinel License Manager service is started. Go to Start->Control Panel->Administrative Tools->Services and locate "Sentinel LM". The status should report the service is started. If it is not started, i.e. blank, right-click/double-click on the "Sentinel LM" service name and select "Start". If the service will not start, one possible cause could be the Sentinel License Manager was previously installed elsewhere, but has since been removed and installed into a different directory. If that is the case, go to Start->Programs->SPSS Sentinel License Manager->Service Loader. Next, ensure the "Executable Path" is correct and click "Add". Finally, start the "Sentinel LM" service following the aforementioned steps.

(3) Select 'Applications' entry.
(4) Select 'IBM' icon.
(5) Select 'SPSS' folder icon.
(6) Select folder icon corresponding to the product (example: 'Statistics')
(7) Select the folder corresponding to the product version (example: '24').
(8) Launch 'License Authorization Wizard' program.
(9) Select the 'License my product now' option.
(10) Select 'Next'.
(11) In the lower left section of this window will appear 'Lock Code for this machine is'. Note the indicated lock code.
(12) Select the 'Cancel button'.
(13) Select the 'Yes' button. The License Authorization program will close.
- `E2.S6`: License Manager
- `E2.S7`: License Manager on Windows Operating Systems
(1a) Open an Administrator Command Prompt. 
(1b) The Command Prompt title bar must read 'Administrator: Command Prompt' or the procedure may not execute properly.
(2a) Change directory ('cd') to the License Manager installation directory. 
(2b) If unsure as to the location of the License Manager installation directory, see TechNote 1989514 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21989514].
(3) Execute the following command: echoid
(4) The response will include a value associated with 'Locking code 1'.
(5) This is the License Manager lock code.

- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I am trying to start SPSS for Windows and I receive the following errors:
- `E3.S3`: The current license does not permit this job to continue.
- `E3.S4`: followed by...
- `E3.S5`: Error # 7003
The license for SPSS for Windows has expired.
This command not executed.
- `E3.S6`: Specific symptom number: 213
- `E3.S7`: What is the problem?
- `E3.S8`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
IF the product presenting the error 7003/symptom 213 is licensed via the Sentinel RMS License Manager, THEN refer to KnowledgeBase resolution 91720.
IF the product presenting error 7003/symptom 213 is licensed with a Single-User or Site license authorization code, THEN go to (A).
- `E3.S9`: (A)
IF your was working normally for more than 14 days prior to presenting error 7003/symptom 213, THEN go to (B)
IF your product has been working for no more than 14 days prior to presenting error 7003/symptom 213, THEN go to (E)
- `E3.S10`: (B) 
Confirm the date and time on the computer are correct.
- `E3.S11`: IF date/time is NOT correct, THEN got to (C)
IF date/time is correct, THEN go to (D).
- `E3.S12`: (C)
1) Reset the date/time on the computer.
2) Start the IBM SPSS product.
- `E3.S13`: IF the error message persists, THEN go to (D)
IF the error not longer presents, then the problem has been resolved.
- `E3.S14`: (D)
1) Delete (or rename) the file named 'lservrc' found in program installation directory of the IBM SPSS product. 
2) License the IBM SPSS product using the License Authorization Wizard and your product authorization code.
- `E3.S15`: (E)
1) Please contact IBM SPSS Customer Service via email at spsscs@us.ibm.com or via phone at 800-521-1337.
2) Provide IBM SPSS Customer Service with the license authorization code used to license your IBM SPSS product.
3) Request confirmation that the license authorization code is for the correct product.
4) Request confirmation that the license authorization code includes the 'base' module (if applicable).
5) Request confirmation that the license authorization code is not expired

Select the Paste menu option.

- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E5.S2`: QUESTION
 Where is the Microsoft Installer (*.msi) file required for unattended/silent/push installations the IBM SPSS Statistics application?
- `E5.S3`: ANSWER
The Microsoft Installer (*.msi) file for IBM SPSS Statistics applications is not available as a separate download. Accessing the.msi file for IBM SPSS Statistics is dependent upon the installation media you have received.
Using the Software Download: 
1. Download and save the installer executable (e.g. 'SPSS_Statistics_24_win64.exe') to a known, accessible location on the computer hard drive.
2. Next, you will need to use the /b switch from your command prompt to extract the .msi file. 
In the example below the SPSS_Statistics_24_win64.exe was downloaded to the C: drive. 
Provide the file location for the extraction. This example uses the directory "MSItest" on the C: drive:
- `E5.S4`: C:\>SPSS_Statistics_24_win64.exe /b"C:\MSItest"
- `E5.S5`: 3. Notice that running this command will launch the InstallShield Wizard. Let this run until the .msi has been extracted. You will see "Extracting: IBM SPSS Statistics 24.msi" message from the installer. You do not need to proceed with the full installation.
- `E5.S6`: Using Installation Media (CD/DVD)
1. Insert the disk.
2. IF prompted to install the software, select 'Cancel'.
3. Browse to the media location. 
4. Open the 'SPSSStatistics' folder.
- `E5.S7`: The 32-bit MSI file will be located in the 'win32'. folder.
The 64-bit MSI file will be located in the 'win64' folder.
- `E5.S8`: Using a compressed (.zip) file
1. Extract (decompress) the contents of the ZIP file into a designated folder.
2. The MSI folder will located in the designated folder.
- `E5.S9`: For documentation on IBM SPSS-specific commands for use with MSI files, see 'Administrator's Guide' appropriate to your license type (e.g. 'Site', 'Concurrent' Users Guide').

## techqa_DEV_Q259#row-0155

Question:
Subnodes are still present on TEP after unconfiguring SOA DC After unconfiguring the ITCAM for SOA DC via the unconfig.sh script, I can still see SOA subnodes and workspaces on TEP.The Websphere instances were restarted and are no longer collecting data and forwarding to the D4 agent.I have shut down the ITCAM agent and deleted the offline entries for the managed systems, but the subnodes appear back once you restart the ITCAM agent.How can I remove them?

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, it seems that even after unconfiguring the ITCAM for SOA DC and deleting offline entries for managed systems, the SOA subnodes still reappear once the ITCAM agent is restarted. To fully remove these subnodes, you can follow these steps:

1. Stop the SOA Agent.
2. Right-click on the SOA subnodes in the TEP console and choose "Clear offline entry" to make them invisible.
3. Remove the information of the deleted entries from the KD4.dc.properties file located in <ITM_HOME>/TMAITM6/KD4/config on Windows or <ITM_HOME>/<platform>/d4/KD4/config on Unix. Save the changes.
4. Delete the persist directory located in <ITM_HOME>/TMAITM6/KD4/logs/KD4.DCA.CACHE/persist on Windows or <ITM_HOME>/<platform>/d4/KD4/logs/KD4.DCA.CACHE/persist on Unix to erase old records.
5. Start the SOA Agent.
6. The deleted SOA subnodes should no longer appear in the TEP console after completing these steps.

Reference evidence:
- `2g`: ** Removing SOA node entry from TEPS workspace **  1.
- `2h`: Stop SOA Agent.  2.
- `2i`: 2nd mouse click on the node entry that you want to remove, choose "Clear offline entry".
- `2k`: Delete the information of the entry (removed from 2 above) from KD4.dc.properties file.
- `2l`: (Windows: <ITM_HOME>\TMAITM6\KD4\config, Unix:<ITM_HOME>/<Platform>/d4/KD4/config), and save it.
- `2m`: The "information of the entry" to be removed (from KD4.dc.properties) would look similiar to this : 8.<DP hostname>.monitor=on 8.<DP hostname>.log=error 8.<DP hostname>.trace=off 8.<DP hostname>.control.count=1 8.<DP hostname>.control.1=*;*;*;*;*;none 8.<DP hostname>.filter.control.count=0  4.
- `2n`: Remove following directory to erase old records which are remembered in this directory. <SOA_BASE_DIR>/KD4/logs/KD4.DCA.CACHE/persist where..
- `2o`: <SOA_BASE_DIR> = (<ITM_HOME>\TMAITM6 in Windows, <ITM_HOME>/<platform>/d4 in Unix)  5.
- `2p`: Start SOA Agent.  6.
- `2q`: From TEPS view, you should be able to see that the deleted entry is gone. PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM

=== CANDIDATE A ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: CAMSOAALL CAMSOATEPDATA same node leaf delete SOA TEPS workspace entry TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: THIS DOCUMENT APPLIES ONLY TO THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE VERSION(S):
 US English
- `E1.S3`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Need to remove the nodes with same name (there are several node names which is the same) and leave only 1 node name in TEPS tree view.
- `E1.S4`: SYMPTOM
Several different causes can result in the following issues.
- `E1.S5`: Issue A : Same node names exist and you want to remove all the same-named nodes and leave only 1 in tree.
- `E1.S6`: Issue B : Individual leaf (node) names for different devices. The individual leaf nodes are with the same name and only one of which reports activity.
- `E1.S7`: CAUSE
Issue B : Mostly it is due to the too long hostnames /long and similar starting server names.
- `E1.S8`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E1.S9`: Issue A. (see symptom above for description)
- `E1.S10`: Here is how to remove/trim the same node name down to 1 node (with the name) left in TEPS view.
- `E1.S11`: 1. Stop the SOA Agent. 
2. Click (with 2nd mouse) the subnode that you want to remove, and choose "Clear offline entry" 
3. From KD4.dc.properties file, remove all the entry about the host/server that you deleted from TEPS and save it.
- `E1.S12`: Example : If you deleted the entry related to Data Power, the related entry (to be removed) looks like this.
8.<DP hostname>.monitor=on
8.<DP hostname>.log=error
8.<DP hostname>.trace=off
8.<DP hostname>.control.count=1
8.<DP hostname>.control.1=*;*;*;*;*;none
8.<DP hostname>.filter.control.count=0
- `E1.S13`: 4. Remove (windows: <ITM_HOME>\TMAITM6\KD4\logs\KD4.DCA.CACHE\persist, unix: <ITM_HOME>/<platform>/d4/KD4/logs/KD4.DCA.CACHE\persist) directory.
- `E1.S14`: 5. Restart SOA Agent.

- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
- `E3.S3`: In the TEP console, most of the applications under the Application Management Console > Applications node in the Navigator tree are offline. Where do these applications come from, and how do you remove the offline applications from this view?
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
- `E3.S5`: In the Physical view, navigate to the AMC (Application Management Console) node in the Navigator tree, and open the Applications link. Notice that a number of applications are offline.
- `E3.S6`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502342&amp;aid=1]
- `E3.S7`: These offline applications are mostly applications that are defined by default by the ITCAM for Transactions agents that you have installed. These default applications are normally shown as offline, because you have not defined a profile to start these applications and collect data.
- `E3.S8`: Note that some of these applications may be shown offline because they were created for testing purposes and are no longer used. Other applications are shown as offline because these are active applications that are actually offline.
- `E3.S9`: For example, open the AMC Editor by clicking the AMC Editor icon in the TEP toolbar.
- `E3.S10`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502342&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502342&aid=2]
- `E3.S11`: Select Applications from the drop-down list. Note that this is the default selection when you open the AMC Editor. The applications listed here are mostly the default applications. These applications were added when you installed or upgraded the ITCAM for Transactions agents. The application names also appear in the Applications list in the TEP Navigator tree..
- `E3.S12`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502342&amp;aid=3]
- `E3.S13`: In the TEP Navigator tree, one at a time, right-click these offline entries. Select the command Clear offline entry. For example:
- `E3.S14`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502342&amp;aid=4]
- `E3.S15`: The offline entry is removed from the TEP Navigator tree. Note that the Clear offline entry command only makes the entry invisible. The applications that you clear become visible again when they come back online.
- `E3.S16`: Caution: The Delete command removes the workspace, not the item. Use Clear offline entry to remove an item.
- `E3.S17`: At this time, you have to select and clear these offline entries one at a time. You cannot select a group of offline entries and clear the group by selecting the Clear offline entry command.
- `E3.S18`: Alternative: You can use the tacmd cleanMS command to clear offline managed systems. The command clears all offline entries in a single step. Offline entries are not displayed again until the applications come back online. Note that you must login to the TEMS using the tacmd login command before running the tacmd cleanMS command.

- `E4.S1`: v2240rlsnotes RELEASE NOTES
- `E4.S2`: ABSTRACT
 In rare cases, a permissions issue could cause the ITCAM WebSphere Application Server agent uninstall to fail.
- `E4.S3`: CONTENT
Problem: In cases where the ITCAM monitoring agent uninstall is not successful, the WebSphere Application Servers that were being monitored will no longer start. This happens when ITCAM for WAS configuration parameters defined in each application server do not get removed when the unconfiguration portion of the uninstall fails.
- `E4.S4`: Resolution: There are two possible solutions for this issue.
1. Deploy the System Monitoring for WebSphere Application Server again. Once the shared service is deployed, attempt the uninstall again.
2. Manually remove the WebSphere Application Server configuration that is specific to ITCAM and is causing this issue. For information about manual removal, refer to the ITCAM topic the Related Information below.
- `E4.S5`: RELATED INFORMATION
 ITCAM [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SS3JRN_7.2.0/com.ibm.itcamfapps_soa.doc_72/soa_install_guide/manuallyremovingdatacollector.html]
- `E5.S1`: 71AMCON-CONF; 71AMCON-WV; 71ISM-WV TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Using ITCAM for Tx with ISM agent monitoring solution, ISM subnode applications are missing in the TEP GUI, under AMC Application Management Console -> "Internet Services" list
- `E5.S3`: SYMPTOM
Looking at the TEP portal GUI, under the AMC T3 agent dashboard node -> Application Management Console -> "Internet Services", in the "All Internet Services profiles" workspace, it contains a list of Profiles.
- `E5.S4`: But when selecting one of them, and mouse click on it, you get a popup window titled "Target not found" that says:
- `E5.S5`: "KFWITM081E the link target can not be found, the link definition might be incorrect or the target is unavailable."
- `E5.S6`: CAUSE
This link target that you used/selected is using actually AMC T3 agent monitoring data associated with the "internet Service profile", and collected by the ISM agent.
- `E5.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
- Check if your AMC Internet Services list is incomplete, several profiles (server subnodes actually corresponding to monitoring application data) are possibly missing.
- `E5.S8`: - Check in the TEP under navigator view, at the bottom of it, if you see a message stating :
- `E5.S9`: "KFWITM024I 1 Navigator update pending"
- `E5.S10`: and check the Hub local time seen there, to compare it with the StartTime of some listed profiles.
- `E5.S11`: - Under ISM node -> Internet Service Monitors -> Profile Statistics -> Profile
- `E5.S12`: verify the !StartTime! of your profiles visible there, to cross check that StartTime are fairly recent for some listed profiles.
- `E5.S13`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
This problem should be gone, after you waited long enough until the AMC agent will have been able to collect the actual first monitoring data from the ISM agent(s) for these "newly created/ started" ISM profiles.
- `E5.S14`: If the AMC Data collection is set currently to 15 minutes, every time you create a new ISM profile, it will take up to 15 minutes before the monitoring data and its subnodes and monitoring results associated to this new profile will be available in the TEP workspaces.
- `E5.S15`: PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM
 itcam itcam for transactions itcam4tx itcamfortx internet services monitoring

   (<ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.cfg or
   <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.xml).
- `E4.S6`: LOCAL FIX
 *  Local Fix/Workaround:
   Reconfigure agent to have exactly same node id
   as value in CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID. Or manually set it
   in following files:
   - for 6.2 release: KYN_ALT_NODEID property in
     <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.cfg file
   - for 7.1 release: value in <altNodeId> tag in
     <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.xml file to new value
   <altNodeId>vrt0085</altNodeId> ).
- `E4.S7`: Restart the agent and verify TEP workspaces.
- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ***************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: Agent for WebSphere in ITCAM for WebSphere
   * V6.2 and ITCAM for Application Diagnostics 7.1 users who
   * set CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID in agent configuration file.
   ***************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:
   * TEP workspaces are blank on agent level (for example
   * Application Server Status workspace). This happens when value
   * of CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID property in yn.ini is different than
   * agent node id set in agent configuration file:
   * v6.2: <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.cfg,
   * v7.1: <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.xml.
   ***************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: Use ITCAM for WebSphere 6.2 FP6, Interim
   * Fix 1, TEMA (6.2.0.6-TIV-ITCAM_WAS_TEMA-IF001) or newer
   * release which contains this fix to resolve this issue.
   ***************************************************************
- `E4.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Setting CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID causes registration on TEMS under
   Managed System Name like: <CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID>:<hostname>:KYNA.
   However, TEMA has it's own setting for agent ID called
   'Alternative Node ID' which is stored in
   <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.cfg or
   <ITM_HOME>/config/<hostname>_yn.xml files. This value is
   used to build internal identification similar to Managed System
   Name.
   When CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID is different than 'Alternative Node ID'
   then TEMA drops request from ITM as those request are for agent
   with CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID name and TEMA identifies it's name as
   value of 'Alternative Node ID'.
- `E4.S10`: The fix for this APAR introduces the precedence of agent node ID
   configurations. If CTIRA_SUBSYSTEM_ID value is present in
   <ITM_HOME>/config/yn.ini file then it overrides value of
   'Alternative Node ID'.
- `E4.S11`: The fix for this APAR is contained in the following maintenance
   packages:
- `E4.S12`: | interim fix | 6.2.0.6-TIV-ITCAM_WAS_TEMA-IF001
     | interim fix | 7.1.0.3-TIV-ITCAMAD-IF0005

## techqa_DEV_Q085#row-0020

Question:
Event Dashboard breaks with Japanese filter Event Dashboard breaks when a filter is created with the browser language set to Japanese. This issue occurs in WebGUI 8.1 Fix Pack 11. 

Reference / gold answer:
To address the issue of the Event Dashboard breaking when a filter is created with the browser language set to Japanese in WebGUI 8.1 Fix Pack 11, you can follow the steps outlined in the APAR STATUS section of the provided context.

The APAR for this issue is JR46703, which affects BPM ADVANCED on version 8.0.1.0. The problem description states that when users with Non-English locales (e.g. ja_JP) for their browsers access Process Portal, the Dashboards do not display the Pie-Chart and Task lists.

The local fix suggested is to temporarily set the browser language preference to English, access the dashboard, and then change it back to the real locale, such as Japanese. This workaround should help resolve the issue until a permanent fix is implemented.

The problem was addressed by adding a configurable flag that resolves the user's browser locale to a Portal-supported locale and properly sets the language as their User Preference. If the user's browser locale is not a Portal-supported locale, then the user's locale will default to English.

To resolve this issue permanently, you can download the fix package from FixCentral. The fix information including install instructions will be available in the readme.txt file provided with the fix package.

Reference evidence:


=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E2.S1`: mobile device; event list; event viewer; omnibus webgui TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 Is it possible to display an event list directly on a mobile device, without drilling down from an Event Dashboard or Gauge?
- `E2.S3`: ANSWER
Yes, it is. The URL can be entered in this format to display an event list in the Event Viewer on a mobile device:
[https]://<host>:<port>/ibm/console/webtop/m/eventviewer?filtername=Escalated&filtertype=global
- `E2.S4`: Note: it is not possible to use a transient filter in the URL under these circumstances. The filter specified must be pre-defined via the Filter Builder.
- `E3.S1`: Health Dashboard; Event viewer; gauge; web gui TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The event list in the Event Viewer is not updated when clicking on gauges in the Netcool Health Dashboard when using Internet Explorer 9 or 10. When using IE11 or Firefox the problem is not seen.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
Step to reproduce:
- `E3.S4`: 1. Log into DASH and open the Health Dashboard
2. Ensure that the event list shown is the Event Viewer, not the AEL
3. Ensure that the active view is the Self Monitoring view
5. Click on a selection of gauges.
- `E3.S5`: Expected result: The event list is updated to show the events which match the related filter (if any such events exist).
- `E3.S6`: Actual result: No update from the Event Viewer. The same events are showing.
- `E3.S7`: CAUSE
This third party API:
- `E3.S8`: var xmlDoc = new ActiveXObject( "Microsoft.XMLDOM" );
- `E3.S9`: in /ibm/console/webtop/scripts/ajax.js causes an exception with some IE9/IE10 browsers.
Stepping over the above line throws the following exception:
eventTransformer: Exception caught while attempting to read payload. Error was:Automation server can't create object
- `E3.S10`: The issue is caused by configuration changes on some Windows machines and is not a defect in OMNIbus Web GUI.
- `E3.S11`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Go to:
- `E3.S12`: " IE9/10 > Internet Options > Security > Custom Level" and set
1. "Run ActiveX controls and plug-ins" to Enable
2. "Script ActiveX controls marked safe for scripting" to Enable

- `E1.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  In SAML Web SSO, when the redirect target is null,
   "INTERNAL ERROR: Please contact your support." is displayed
   in the browser.  There is no information in the FFDC or
   SystemOut.log for problem diagnosis.
- `E1.S5`: LOCAL FIX
- `E1.S6`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  IBM WebSphere Application Server users of   *
   *                  SAML Web SSO                                *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Additional diagnostics are required     *
   *                      when the SAML Web SSO redirect URL is   *
   *                      null                                    *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:  Install a fix pack that contains this       *
   *                  APAR.                                       *
   ****************************************************************
   In SAML Web SSO, when the redirect target is null, the runtime
   sets the redirect target to NO_TARGET.  This results in
   "INTERNAL ERROR: Please contact your support." being displayed
   in the browser.
   .
   There should be some indication in the SystemOut.log that this
   condition has happened so that the administrator can attempt
   to address the issue.
- `E1.S7`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The SAML Web SSO TAI is updated to redirect to the configured
   error page when the redirect target is null.
   .
   When the redirect target is null, the following error message
   will appear in the SystemOut.log file:
   .
   CWSML7035E: The SAML Web Single Sign-on (SSO) Trust
   Association Interceptor (TAI) is unable to determine a
   redirect target URL. The redirect URL can come from the
   sso_<id>.sp.targetUrl SAML TAI custom property, the RelayState
   parameter in the SAMLResponse or the WasSamlSpReqUrl cookie.
   If you do not intend to have a value for the
   sso_<id>.sp.targetUrl SAML TAI custom property or have your
   IdP send a RelayState parameter in the SAMLResponse, then
   check earlier in the log to see if you have a CWSML7036W
   warning that indicates that the request URL host name is not
   the same as the ACS URL host name. If you see that warning,
   then that condition must be corrected to fix this error. The
   value for the relayState parameter on the SAMLResponse is [{0}].
   .
   EXPLANATION: The SAML Web SSO TAI cannot find a redirect URL
   for the current request.  The redirect URL can come from three
   places: 1) the sso_<id>.sp.targetUrl SAML TAI custom property,
   2) the RelayState parameter in the SAMLResponse and 3) the
   WasSamlSpReqUrl cookie. At least one of these three things
   must be present in order for the SAML TAI to be able to
   determine the redirect URL. In this case, none of these three
   things are present, therefore, the SAML TAI can not determine
   the redirect URL. Note that the SAML TAI may have set a
   WasSamlSpReqUrl cookie earlier in the process, but the browser
   did not make the cookie available to the SAML TAI.
- `E1.S8`: these three things
   must be present in order for the SAML TAI to be able to
   determine the redirect URL. In this case, none of these three
   things are present, therefore, the SAML TAI can not determine
   the redirect URL. Note that the SAML TAI may have set a
   WasSamlSpReqUrl cookie earlier in the process, but the browser
   did not make the cookie available to the SAML TAI. Also, the
   RelayState parameter must be a URL that uses the http or https
   protocol.
   .
   USER ACTION: Ensure at least one of the following is true: 1)
   the sso_<id>.sp.targetUrl SAML TAI custom property is
   configured for the current SP, 2) the IdP sets the RelayState
   parameter on the SAMLResponse with a valid URL that uses the
   http or https protocol or 3) the WasSamlSpReqUrl cookie is
   made available to the SAML TAI. In order for the
   WasSamlSpReqUrl to be available to the SAML TAI, the original
   request URL must have the same host name as the ACS URL that
   is configured on the sso_<id>.sp.acsUrl TAI custom property.
   .
   .
   The SAML TAI is also updated to check for duplicate acsUrl
   entries at load time.  If any are found, the following warning
   will be emitted:
   .
   CWSML7038W: The SAML Web Single Single Sign-on (SSO) Trust
   Association Interceptor (TAI) has two assertion consumer
   service URL custom properties configured that have the same
   URL path: [{0}] and [{1}].  This condition can cause
   unexpected behavior at run time.  To prevent further issues,
   all text after <hostname>:<port> must be unique for each
   [sso_<id>.sp.acsUrl] custom property value.
   .
   EXPLANATION: The value for each SAML [sso_<id>.sp.acsUrl]
   custom property must have a unique URL path.  A URL path does
   not include the protocol and <hostname>:<port> parts of a URL
   string.  For example, although the URL strings for
   https://somewhere.ibm.com/samlsps/hello/app and
   https://elsewhere.ibm.com/samlsps/hello/app are different, the
   URL paths are the same.  If two acsUrl entries have the same
   URL path, when a SAMLResponse is sent to one of the URLs that
   has a duplicate path, the service provider that is chosen to
   handle the request will be indeterminate.
   .
   USER ACTION: Ensure that the URL configured for each of the
   [so_<id>.sp.acsUrl] custom properties have unique URL paths,
   meaning that they have unique text after the <hostname>:<port>
   part of the URL string.

- `E4.S1`: mobile device; event list; event viewer; omnibus webgui TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 Is it possible to display an event list directly on a mobile device, without drilling down from an Event Dashboard or Gauge?
- `E4.S3`: ANSWER
Yes, it is. The URL can be entered in this format to display an event list in the Event Viewer on a mobile device:
[https]://<host>:<port>/ibm/console/webtop/m/eventviewer?filtername=Escalated&filtertype=global
- `E4.S4`: Note: it is not possible to use a transient filter in the URL under these circumstances. The filter specified must be pre-defined via the Filter Builder.

   filesets need to be added to the WebSphere Application Server

   management tool, or not installed.

## techqa_DEV_Q149#row-0050

Question:
Why SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above? Why SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above? The same configuration works on v7.2. 

Reference / gold answer:
SSH connections fail after upgrading to v7.5.2 and above because the default set of ciphers and MACs have been altered in OpenSSH releases starting from version 6.7. Unsafe algorithms such as CBC ciphers and arcfour are disabled by default in these versions. If the SSH client or server being used is older and does not support the safer algorithms enabled by default in v7.5.2 and above, the connection will fail. To resolve this issue, either upgrade the SSH client/server to a version that supports the safe algorithms or modify the OpenSSH configuration file to add back the unsafe algorithms temporarily.

Reference evidence:
- `0c`: This will only happen where the partner SSH server or client on the connection is running a very old version of the SSH / OpenSSH code. SYMPTOM
- `0d`: Errors on connection with "No matching cipher found", or "No matching MAC algorithm found", or occasionally "No matching kex algorithm found". CAUSE
- `0k`: In OpenSSH 6.7 and subsequent releases, changes were made to the default set of ciphers.
- `0l`: The release notes at http://www.openssh.com/txt/release-6.7 [http://www.openssh.com/txt/release-6.7] state the following:
- `0m`: Changes since OpenSSH 6.6 ========================= Potentially-incompatible changes
- `0n`: * sshd(8): The default set of ciphers and MACs has been altered to
- `0o`: remove unsafe algorithms.
- `0p`: In particular, CBC ciphers and arcfour*
- `0q`: are disabled by default.
- `0t`: If the SSH client/SSH server is older and does not yet support the safer ciphers and MACs, and wants to use one of the unsafe ciphers/MACs disabled by default, the connection will fail.
- `0w`: OpenSSH 6.9p1 has the following algorithms available as default.
- `0y`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `0z`: There are two potential solutions to this issue.
- `0aa`: From a security viewpoint, Option 1 must be preferred as it uses the secure algorithms and does not introduce back in unsafe algorithms.
- `0ad`: Upgrade the SSH client/server to a version where it uses the safe algorithms in the default lists above.
- `0ae`: Refer to your SSH client/server provider for information on how to do this, and which version you will need. 2.
- `3n`:  *  Disabled diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1 and diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 algorithms by default.
- `3o`: Disabled MD5-based MAC algorithms.
- `3ay`:    Default KEX algorithms  * curve25519-sha256@libssh.org
- `3az`:     *

- `3bb`:     *

- `3bd`:     *

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Applying PTFs to 5733SC1 (OpenSSH) can cause SSH/SFTP/SCP connections to fail with error messages in regards to not matching ciphers. This will only happen where the partner SSH server or client on the connection is running a very old version of the SSH / OpenSSH code.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
Errors on connection with "No matching cipher found", or "No matching MAC algorithm found", or occasionally "No matching kex algorithm found".
- `E1.S4`: CAUSE
The following PTFs, or their supersedes, upgrade OpenSSH on the IBM i from an earlier release to 6.9p1:
- `E1.S5`: o R610 - SI57920 (1000)
o R710 - SI57762 (5317) 
o R720 - SI57771 (5310)
- `E1.S6`: Important Note: The R710 and R720 PTFs are on a cumulative package; therefore, applying that package will also upgrade OpenSSH.
- `E1.S7`: The previous release of OpenSSH on these releases was 6.6p1. In OpenSSH 6.7 and subsequent releases, changes were made to the default set of ciphers. The release notes at http://www.openssh.com/txt/release-6.7 [http://www.openssh.com/txt/release-6.7] state the following:
- `E1.S8`: Changes since OpenSSH 6.6
=========================
- `E1.S9`: Potentially-incompatible changes
- `E1.S10`: * sshd(8): The default set of ciphers and MACs has been altered to
remove unsafe algorithms. In particular, CBC ciphers and arcfour*
are disabled by default.
- `E1.S11`: The full set of algorithms remains available if configured
explicitly via the Ciphers and MACs sshd_config options.
- `E1.S12`: If the SSH client/SSH server is older and does not yet support the safer ciphers and MACs, and wants to use one of the unsafe ciphers/MACs disabled by default, the connection will fail.
- `E1.S13`: Issues have also been seen with Key Exchange Algorithms (kex) failing on a connection attempt.
- `E1.S14`: NOTE : The upgrade to OpenSSH 6.9p1 was necessary in order to fix several published CVE vulnerabilities in the OpenSSH code and ensure PCI compliance.
- `E1.S15`: ENVIRONMENT
OpenSSH 6.9p1 has the following algorithms available as default. This information is taken from the OpenSSH manual page [http://www.openbsd.org/cgi-bin/man.cgi/OpenBSD-current/man5/sshd_config.5?query=sshd_config&sec=5] for sshd_config:
- `E1.S16`: Ciphers
- `E1.S17`: chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com, 
aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr, 
aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com
- `E1.S18`: MACs
- `E1.S19`: umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com, 
hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com, 
umac-64@openssh.com,umac-128@openssh.com, 
hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512
- `E1.S20`: KexAlgorithms
- `E1.S21`: curve25519-sha256@libssh.org, 
ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521, 
diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, 
diffie-hellman-group14-sha1
- `E1.S22`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
There are two potential solutions to this issue. From a security viewpoint, Option 1 must be preferred as it uses the secure algorithms and does not introduce back in unsafe algorithms. Unsafe means that security vulnerabilities have been found in the algorithms being used. Option 2 is recommended only as a stop-gap to allow time to upgrade the client or server software, and then you should remove the changes from the configuration file:
- `E1.S23`: 1. Upgrade the SSH client/server to a version where it uses the safe algorithms in the default lists above. Refer to your SSH client/server provider for information on how to do this, and which version you will need.
- `E1.S24`: 2. Modify the appropriate OpenSSH configuration file on the IBM i to add back in the unsafe algorithms required to have the client connect.
- `E1.S25`: If the IBM i is the SSH Server, modify the sshd_config file
- `E1.S26`: If the IBM i is the SSH Client, modify the ssh_config file
- `E1.S27`: The configuration file will be found in the following locations per release:
- `E1.S28`: V6R1 - /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/openssh-3.8.1p1/etc/ 
V7R1 - /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/openssh-4.7p1/etc/ 
V7R2+ - /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/
- `E1.S29`: Using WRKLNK, locate the file, and select Option 2 (=Edit) against it.

=== CANDIDATE B ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Applying PTFs to 5733SC1 (OpenSSH) can cause SSH/SFTP/SCP connections to fail with error messages in regards to not matching ciphers. This will only happen where the partner SSH server or client on the connection is running a very old version of the SSH / OpenSSH code.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
Errors on connection with "No matching cipher found", or "No matching MAC algorithm found", or occasionally "No matching kex algorithm found".
- `E1.S4`: CAUSE
The following PTFs, or their supersedes, upgrade OpenSSH on the IBM i from an earlier release to 6.9p1:
- `E1.S5`: o R610 - SI57920 (1000)
o R710 - SI57762 (5317) 
o R720 - SI57771 (5310)
- `E1.S6`: Important Note: The R710 and R720 PTFs are on a cumulative package; therefore, applying that package will also upgrade OpenSSH.
- `E1.S7`: The previous release of OpenSSH on these releases was 6.6p1. In OpenSSH 6.7 and subsequent releases, changes were made to the default set of ciphers. The release notes at http://www.openssh.com/txt/release-6.7 [http://www.openssh.com/txt/release-6.7] state the following:
- `E1.S8`: Changes since OpenSSH 6.6
=========================
- `E1.S9`: Potentially-incompatible changes
- `E1.S10`: * sshd(8): The default set of ciphers and MACs has been altered to
remove unsafe algorithms. In particular, CBC ciphers and arcfour*
are disabled by default.
- `E1.S11`: The full set of algorithms remains available if configured
explicitly via the Ciphers and MACs sshd_config options.
- `E1.S12`: If the SSH client/SSH server is older and does not yet support the safer ciphers and MACs, and wants to use one of the unsafe ciphers/MACs disabled by default, the connection will fail.
- `E1.S13`: Issues have also been seen with Key Exchange Algorithms (kex) failing on a connection attempt.
- `E1.S14`: NOTE : The upgrade to OpenSSH 6.9p1 was necessary in order to fix several published CVE vulnerabilities in the OpenSSH code and ensure PCI compliance.
- `E1.S15`: ENVIRONMENT
OpenSSH 6.9p1 has the following algorithms available as default. This information is taken from the OpenSSH manual page [http://www.openbsd.org/cgi-bin/man.cgi/OpenBSD-current/man5/sshd_config.5?query=sshd_config&sec=5] for sshd_config:
- `E1.S16`: Ciphers
- `E1.S17`: chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com, 
aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr, 
aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com
- `E1.S18`: MACs
- `E1.S19`: umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com, 
hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com, 
umac-64@openssh.com,umac-128@openssh.com, 
hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512
- `E1.S20`: KexAlgorithms
- `E1.S21`: curve25519-sha256@libssh.org, 
ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521, 
diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, 
diffie-hellman-group14-sha1
- `E1.S22`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
There are two potential solutions to this issue. From a security viewpoint, Option 1 must be preferred as it uses the secure algorithms and does not introduce back in unsafe algorithms. Unsafe means that security vulnerabilities have been found in the algorithms being used. Option 2 is recommended only as a stop-gap to allow time to upgrade the client or server software, and then you should remove the changes from the configuration file:
- `E1.S23`: 1. Upgrade the SSH client/server to a version where it uses the safe algorithms in the default lists above. Refer to your SSH client/server provider for information on how to do this, and which version you will need.
- `E1.S24`: 2. Modify the appropriate OpenSSH configuration file on the IBM i to add back in the unsafe algorithms required to have the client connect.
- `E1.S25`: If the IBM i is the SSH Server, modify the sshd_config file
- `E1.S26`: If the IBM i is the SSH Client, modify the ssh_config file
- `E1.S27`: The configuration file will be found in the following locations per release:
- `E1.S28`: V6R1 - /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/openssh-3.8.1p1/etc/ 
V7R1 - /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/openssh-4.7p1/etc/ 
V7R2+ - /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/
- `E1.S29`: Using WRKLNK, locate the file, and select Option 2 (=Edit) against it.

Visible answer:
For IBM i, the relevant PTFs upgraded OpenSSH from 6.6p1 to 6.9p1; the upgrade was made to address published CVE vulnerabilities and PCI compliance. [E1.S4] [E1.S5] [E1.S7] [E1.S14]

[
  {
    "text": "SSH connections fail after the upgrade because the newer SSH implementation changes the default cipher, MAC, and sometimes key-exchange algorithm lists, disabling unsafe legacy algorithms such as CBC ciphers and arcfour.   {
    "text": "The preferred fix is to upgrade the remote SSH client or server so that it supports the safer default algorithms.
