- `E3.S1`: rsa; rsm; rsd; RDA; RPT; RFT; RMT; RDBe; RAD; perm; permanent; temp; real; license; key; temporary; licensing; trial; ga; version; 1254371; SDP; RMC; Import Product Activation Kit; Configure Floating License Support TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 How do you change the trial download into a permanently licensed product after you have installed the evaluation version of an IBM Rational Software Development Platform desktop product, such as Rational Software Architect?
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
Trial version of Rational software products can be converted to the permanent licensed products by applying/enabling the permanent license key over a evaluation key.
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
Follow the instructions below to install the activation kit or to enable floating license keys. The product activation kits contain the permanent license key for converting a trial Rational product.
- `E3.S5`: After you download a product activation kit, you must import the kit from the download location by using IBM Installation Manager.
- `E3.S6`: Note: IBM Rational Method Composer uses the product activation kit, license keys and the IBM Installation Manager as of version 7.2 and 7.5, but it does not support floating license keys.
- `E3.S7`: To import an activation kit and enable the new license key
- `E3.S8`: 1. Start IBM Installation Manager.
- `E3.S9`: 2. On the main page, click Manage Licenses.
- `E3.S10`: 3. On the Install Packages page, select a package and click Import product enablement kit.
- `E3.S11`: 4. Click Next. 
    Details for the selected package are displayed, including the current license kind and the version range to which the license applies.
- `E3.S12`: 5. Browse to the path of the download location for the kit, then select the appropriate Java archive (JAR) file and click Open.
- `E3.S13`: 6. Click Next. The Summary page displays the target install directory for the activation kit, the product the new license applies to, and version information.
- `E3.S14`: 7. Click Finish.
- `E3.S15`: To enable floating license keys
- `E3.S16`: 1. Start IBM Installation Manager.
- `E3.S17`: 2. On the main page, click Manage Licenses.
- `E3.S18`: 3. On the Install Packages page, select a version of a package, click Configure license servers, and click Next.
- `E3.S19`: 4. On the License Servers page, select the Enable Rational Common Licensing check box.
- `E3.S20`: 5. Configure one or more license server connections.  1. Click the Add button. 
     2. In the Add Server window, in the Name field, type the host name of the license server. 
     3. (Optional) In the Port field, type a value for environments where a firewall is used. Do not assign a value to this port unless your administrator instructs you to do so. 
     4. Click OK. 
     5. If your system administrator has given you the host names of additional license servers, repeat the steps to add each server. 
        For a redundant license server configuration (in which three servers are used), type each host name in this format: hostname1, hostname2, hostname3. 
        For each port number, type accordingly: host1port#, host2port#, host3port#.
- `E3.S21`: 6. Click Next.
- `E3.S22`: 7. (Optional) Configure the license usage order for your custom packages. The order of licenses in the list determines the order in which your product attempts to obtain license keys for specific licenses.
- `E3.S23`: 8. Click Finish.
- `E3.S24`: Note: The Manage Licenses wizard indicates whether the floating licenses configuration is successful.
- `E3.S25`: For each port number, type accordingly: host1port#, host2port#, host3port#.
- `E3.S26`: 6. Click Next.
- `E3.S27`: 7. (Optional) Configure the license usage order for your custom packages. The order of licenses in the list determines the order in which your product attempts to obtain license keys for specific licenses.
- `E3.S28`: 8. Click Finish.
- `E3.S29`: Note: The Manage Licenses wizard indicates whether the floating licenses configuration is successful. When you open the enabled product next, a connection is created to the license server to obtain a license key from the pool of available floating license keys.
- `E3.S30`: For the latest version
- `E3.S31`: To enable floating license keys 
 1. In IBM Installation Manager, go to Manage Licenses, then Select the product that you would like import 
 2. Select Configure Floating license support and click Next 
 3. Select Enable floating license enforcement and click on + button 
 4. Select Server type > Add Name > Add Port 
 5. Click on Test Connection > OK 
 6. Select Next > Finish
- `E3.S32`: 1.
- `E3.S33`: To import an activation kit and enable the new license key
- `E3.S34`: 1.  Launch IBM Installation Manager. 
 2.  Click the Manage Licenses button. 
 3.  Highlight the product for which you are importing the activation kit. 
 4.  Click the Import product activation kit radio button. 
 5.  Click Next. 
 6.  Browse to the .jar file and click Next. 
 7.  After reading and accepting the license agreement click Finish. 
 8.  You should receive a message stating that the license import was successful. Click Finish 
 9.  You will now be back on the main page of the Installation Manager. 
 10. Click the Manage Licenses button. 
 11. Highlight the product for which you just imported the activation kit. 
 12. Click the Configure floating license support radio button. 
 13. Click Next. 
 14. Click the Disable floating license enforcement radio button. 
 15. Click Finish.

- `E4.S2`: ABSTRACT
 IBM Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 fix pack release.
- `E4.S3`: DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
The Telelogic Rhapsody version 7.4.0.1 fix pack release is available for download on the IBM FixCentral site.
- `E4.S4`: PREREQUISITES
Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 replaces existing versions of Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4. It is possible to install Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 concurrently with releases prior to 7.4.
- `E4.S5`: Licensing:
The upgrade to Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 is included for all licenses with current maintenance contracts. 
You can now use the License Key Center [https://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/] [https://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/l] to get and manage your keys for Telelogic products. This includes Telelogic software purchases made through IBM as well as for legacy orders through Telelogic AB.
- `E4.S6`: The IBM license agreement entitles users to “borrow” licenses from a floating license server for use offline when disconnected from the server. If you wish to use this capability then you need to obtain a new license file with borrowing enabled.
- `E4.S7`: Users with Rhapsody 7.0 or earlier licenses will need to get a new license to use Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 from the License Key Center [https://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/]

- `E2.S1`: rsa; rsm; rsd; RDA; RPT; RFT; RMT; RDBe; RAD; perm; permanent; temp; real; license; key; temporary; licensing; trial; ga; version; 1254371; SDP; RMC; Import Product Activation Kit; Configure Floating License Support TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 How do you change the trial download into a permanently licensed product after you have installed the evaluation version of an IBM Rational Software Development Platform desktop product, such as Rational Software Architect?
- `E2.S3`: CAUSE
Trial version of Rational software products can be converted to the permanent licensed products by applying/enabling the permanent license key over a evaluation key.
- `E2.S4`: ANSWER
Follow the instructions below to install the activation kit or to enable floating license keys. The product activation kits contain the permanent license key for converting a trial Rational product.
- `E2.S5`: After you download a product activation kit, you must import the kit from the download location by using IBM Installation Manager.
- `E2.S6`: Note: IBM Rational Method Composer uses the product activation kit, license keys and the IBM Installation Manager as of version 7.2 and 7.5, but it does not support floating license keys.
- `E2.S7`: To import an activation kit and enable the new license key
- `E2.S8`: 1. Start IBM Installation Manager.
- `E2.S9`: 2. On the main page, click Manage Licenses.
- `E2.S10`: 3. On the Install Packages page, select a package and click Import product enablement kit.
- `E2.S11`: 4. Click Next. 
    Details for the selected package are displayed, including the current license kind and the version range to which the license applies.
- `E2.S12`: 5. Browse to the path of the download location for the kit, then select the appropriate Java archive (JAR) file and click Open.
- `E2.S13`: 6. Click Next. The Summary page displays the target install directory for the activation kit, the product the new license applies to, and version information.
- `E2.S14`: 7. Click Finish.
- `E2.S15`: To enable floating license keys
- `E2.S16`: 1. Start IBM Installation Manager.
- `E2.S17`: 2. On the main page, click Manage Licenses.
- `E2.S18`: 3. On the Install Packages page, select a version of a package, click Configure license servers, and click Next.
- `E2.S19`: 4. On the License Servers page, select the Enable Rational Common Licensing check box.
- `E2.S20`: 5. Configure one or more license server connections.  1. Click the Add button. 
     2. In the Add Server window, in the Name field, type the host name of the license server. 
     3. (Optional) In the Port field, type a value for environments where a firewall is used. Do not assign a value to this port unless your administrator instructs you to do so. 
     4. Click OK. 
     5. If your system administrator has given you the host names of additional license servers, repeat the steps to add each server. 
        For a redundant license server configuration (in which three servers are used), type each host name in this format: hostname1, hostname2, hostname3. 
        For each port number, type accordingly: host1port#, host2port#, host3port#.
- `E2.S21`: 6. Click Next.
- `E2.S22`: 7. (Optional) Configure the license usage order for your custom packages. The order of licenses in the list determines the order in which your product attempts to obtain license keys for specific licenses.
- `E2.S23`: 8. Click Finish.
- `E2.S24`: Note: The Manage Licenses wizard indicates whether the floating licenses configuration is successful.
- `E2.S25`: For each port number, type accordingly: host1port#, host2port#, host3port#.
- `E2.S26`: 6. Click Next.
- `E2.S27`: 7. (Optional) Configure the license usage order for your custom packages. The order of licenses in the list determines the order in which your product attempts to obtain license keys for specific licenses.
- `E2.S28`: 8. Click Finish.
- `E2.S29`: Note: The Manage Licenses wizard indicates whether the floating licenses configuration is successful. When you open the enabled product next, a connection is created to the license server to obtain a license key from the pool of available floating license keys.
- `E2.S30`: For the latest version
- `E2.S31`: To enable floating license keys 
 1. In IBM Installation Manager, go to Manage Licenses, then Select the product that you would like import 
 2. Select Configure Floating license support and click Next 
 3. Select Enable floating license enforcement and click on + button 
 4. Select Server type > Add Name > Add Port 
 5. Click on Test Connection > OK 
 6. Select Next > Finish
- `E2.S32`: 1.
- `E2.S33`: To import an activation kit and enable the new license key
- `E2.S34`: 1.  Launch IBM Installation Manager. 
 2.  Click the Manage Licenses button. 
 3.  Highlight the product for which you are importing the activation kit. 
 4.  Click the Import product activation kit radio button. 
 5.  Click Next. 
 6.  Browse to the .jar file and click Next. 
 7.  After reading and accepting the license agreement click Finish. 
 8.  You should receive a message stating that the license import was successful. Click Finish 
 9.  You will now be back on the main page of the Installation Manager. 
 10. Click the Manage Licenses button. 
 11. Highlight the product for which you just imported the activation kit. 
 12. Click the Configure floating license support radio button. 
 13. Click Next. 
 14. Click the Disable floating license enforcement radio button. 
 15. Click Finish.

- `E3.S1`: Tools and Utilities; License Feature TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 What are the features incorporated with the "Tools and Utilities" License key for IBM Rational Rhapsody?
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
You would like to know all the features of the Tools and Utilities license key
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
The license features that come incorporated with IBM Rational Rhapsody Tools & Utilities Add on keys are as follows:
- `E3.S5`: * ReporterPro 
 * Reporter 
 * RPGetConnected 
 * RPGetConnectedWind 
 * RPGetConnectedVxw 
 * RPGetConnectedSol 
 * RPGetConnectedN 
 * RPGetConnectedG 
 * RPUNCS 
 * RPTcSEAddon 
 * RPGraphPanel 
 * RPRG 
 * RPRG_DOORS 
 * RPRG_X2TXT 
 * RPRG_REQPRO 
 * RPRG_RP 
 * RPRG_SIMULINK 
 * RPRG_TAGGER 
 * RPRG_CALIBERRM 
 * RPUSimulink 
 * RPXMI 
 * RPTAUXMI
- `E3.S6`: Note: Important functionalities of Rational Rhapsody such as Gateway [ RPRG], Import and Export of XMI files in Rhapsody [RPXMI], Panel Diagrams [RPGraphPanel] and Reporter Plus [ReporterPro] among others are covered
- `E3.S7`: RELATED INFORMATION
 Rational DOORS license features [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21607708]
Rational TAU License features [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21608087]
Rational Build Forge features [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21608803]
Rational Dashboard [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21608812]
- `E4.S1`: fixpack; patch DOWNLOADABLE FILES
- `E4.S2`: ABSTRACT
 IBM Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 fix pack release.
- `E4.S3`: DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
The Telelogic Rhapsody version 7.4.0.1 fix pack release is available for download on the IBM FixCentral site.
- `E4.S4`: PREREQUISITES
Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 replaces existing versions of Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4. It is possible to install Telelogic Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 concurrently with releases prior to 7.4.
- `E4.S5`: Licensing:
The upgrade to Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 is included for all licenses with current maintenance contracts. 
You can now use the License Key Center [https://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/] [https://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/l] to get and manage your keys for Telelogic products. This includes Telelogic software purchases made through IBM as well as for legacy orders through Telelogic AB.
- `E4.S6`: The IBM license agreement entitles users to “borrow” licenses from a floating license server for use offline when disconnected from the server. If you wish to use this capability then you need to obtain a new license file with borrowing enabled.
- `E4.S7`: Users with Rhapsody 7.0 or earlier licenses will need to get a new license to use Rhapsody 7.4.0.1 from the License Key Center [https://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/]

## techqa_DEV_Q039#row-0060

Question:
How do I upgrade my virtual DataPower Appliance from 5.0 firmware to 6.0+ firmware? When attempting to upgrade my Virtual DataPower Appliance from 5.0.0.8 firmware version to 6.0+ firmware versions, I receive a failure message. 

Reference / gold answer:
To upgrade your virtual DataPower Appliance from 5.0 firmware to 6.0+ firmware, follow these steps:

1. If your virtual deployment is at the 5.0.0.8 firmware level, you must first upgrade to 5.0.0.8 or later fix pack before upgrading to 6.0.0.0 or later. The 5.0.0.8 fix pack contains critical fixes necessary for the upgrade.

2. Make sure that you have upgraded to the 5.0.0.8 fix pack or later before attempting to upgrade to 6.0.0.0 or later. 

3. Refer to the Critical Updates document for IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA appliances for guidance when migrating to a later firmware level.

4. Once you have upgraded to the required firmware level, you can proceed with upgrading to 6.0.0.0 or later. 

If you are experiencing failure messages during the upgrade process, refer to the troubleshooting steps provided in the context above. Additionally, you can reach out to DataPower Support for further assistance.

- `E4.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A 9235 appliance may restart or in rare cases the boot up may not complete due to Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) communications loss.
- `E4.S3`: CAUSE
NOTE: DataPower highly recommends upgrading to a version containing the fix for APAR IC80983
- `E4.S4`: A DataPower 9235 appliance may be restarted without a back trace by its hardware watchdog due to a Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) communications loss.
- `E4.S5`: This also rarely causes a failure to restart successfully.
- `E4.S6`: If a failure to restart occurs, the appliance needs to be manually power cycled by removing and then replacing the power cords.
- `E4.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Due to the potential impact of this problem, DataPower highly recommends upgrading to a version containing the fix for APAR IC80983.

Status: `ANSWER`

Visible answer:
Do not install a Fix Central fix pack earlier than 5.0.0.8 when the virtual deployment is at 5.0.0.8 or later. [E3.S14]

The failure occurs because not all scrypt4 fix packs are compatible with the original 5.0.0.0 OVA files; using an incompatible fix pack can cause unexpected errors. [E3.S3]

For a 5.0.0.0 OVA from 29 March 2013, only the 5.0.0.0 and 5.0.0.8-or-later fix packs are supported. For a 5.0.0.0 OVA from 30 November 2012, any Fix Central fix pack except the 5.0.0.0 fix pack can be installed. [E3.S6] [E3.S8]

After reaching 6.0.0.0 or later, do not install any fix pack earlier than 5.0.0.8. [E3.S17]

- `E1.S3`: This firmware image contains the latest VSL 3.2.6 SSD driver. This image includes a firmware driver that is intended for appliances that contain the VSL 3.2.6 or lower version. After you upgrade with this firmware image, the appliance firmware cannot be rolled back to the previous firmware version that you installed for V2.5 Fix Pack 3. Likewise, if you upgrade to this VSL 3.2.6 SSD driver from an existing VSL 3.1.1 SSD driver, then you cannot roll back to the VSL 3.1.1 SSD driver version. However, if you upgrade to a firmware that contains the VSL 3.2.6 SSD driver from an appliance that already contains the VSL 3.2.6 SSD driver, the you can roll back to the previous VSL 3.2.6 firmware version.
- `E1.S4`: Alternatively, use the following table to determine the rollback scenarios for each firmware and driver image:
- `E1.S5`: Begin with SSD driver Upgrade the firmware using driver Rollback available VSL 3.1.1 VSL 3.1.1 Yes VSL 3.1.1 VSL 3.2.6 No VSL 3.2.6 VSL 3.1.1 You must roll back because this scenario causes the system to fail. VSL 3.2.6 VSL 3.2.6 Yes INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS

- `E2.S1`: 2. Following the instructions upgrade documentation in the information center:  * Remove extraneous files 
     * Reboot the appliance to release temporary storage 
     * Transfer the firmware image to the appliance 
     * Install the firmware image
- `E2.S2`: 3. Verify that the appliance has the Data Integration Module.  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Device Features. The list includes:  * Binary processing support 
        * PKCS #7 and S/MIME support 
        * SQL-ODBC support 
        * Database Connectivity Option support
- `E2.S3`: * From the command line, issue the show features command. The list includes:  * DataGlue 
        * PKCS7-SMIME 
        * SQL-ODBC 
        * DCO
- `E2.S4`: Part 5: Installing the firmware image. 
Install the firmware image. XG45 firmware images selectively install only the features licensed for the appliance. In order to make the Data Integration Module features available, the firmware must be upgrade after installing the license image. 
 1. Download the firmware image for your appliance model and licenses from FixCentral 
 2. Upgrade the appliance firmware following the upgrade documentation in the information center 
 3. Repeat part 4 step 3 and ensure all of the licenses are both enabled and available.
- `E2.S5`: If the installation is successful and the list does not include the features for the Data Integration Module, the most likely reason is that the firmware image was for a different appliance. Each firmware image to add the Data Integration Module uses the serial number of the appliance as the key. If you install a downloaded image to a different appliance, you will notice that the firmware is upgraded to that firmware level and that the features for the Data Integration Module are not available.
- `E2.S6`: If you accessed the download site using the Controlled Access Key and installed the downloaded image to the appliance with the matching serial number and the feature list does not include the features for the Data Integration Module, contact IBM Support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322].
- `E2.S7`: Contacting IBM Support 
When reporting the problem to IBM Support, the representative will need your Controlled Access Key in addition to the standard information to include. Go to Contacting IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliances Support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322].

- `E3.S2`: ABSTRACT
 Effective 19 June 2016, IBM will withdraw support for the WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances 6.0 and 6.0.1 firmware levels.
- `E3.S3`: CONTENT
Effective 19 June 2016, IBM will withdraw support for the WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances 6.0 and 6.0.1 firmware levels. See software withdrawal and discontinuance of service announcement letters:
- `E3.S4`: US 915-085 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/5/897/ENUS915-085/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] Canada A15-0304 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/4/649/ENUSA15-0304/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] EMEA ZP15-0207 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/7/877/ENUSZP15-0207/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] AP WP15-0057 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/7/872/ENUSWP15-0057/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] Japan JP15-0206 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/6/760/ENUSJP15-0206/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] LA LP15-0206 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/6/899/ENUSLP15-0206/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en]
- `E3.S5`: Effective 19 June 2016, IBM will withdraw support for firmware level 6.0 and 6.0.1 on the following WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances:
- `E3.S6`: * XG45 (7198-32X, 2426-32X/33X) 
 * XG45 Virtual Edition 
 * XI52 (7199-42X, 2426-42X/43X) 
 * XI52 Virtual Edition 
 * XB62 (7199-62X, 2426-62X/63X)
- `E3.S7`: Note: Standard firmware support (all releases) for the XI50 Blade (MTM 4195-4BX) ends 4/30/2015. See IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliance Support Lifecycle [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21246298] and announcement letter [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/6/897/ENUS913-076/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] 914-067 [http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/7/897/ENUS914-067/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en] for more information.
- `E3.S8`: Customers running firmware level 6.0 or 6.0.1 (or any earlier level) are advised to plan to upgrade to the latest supported releases of WebSphere DataPower firmware in order to continue receiving technical support, as well as proactively avoiding problems that are already resolved. Refer to Supported Firmware versions and recommended upgrade levels [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631] for more information.
- `E3.S9`: IBM recommends that users consider applying the 7.0 or 7.1 latest fixpack version (or later) of the firmware. Of course, in the case of upgrading firmware for any critical embedded system, IBM recommends that users test their configurations and surrounding applications before moving into production. To easily find the latest fixpack levels, please use this link: http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631] .
- `E3.S10`: In addition, refer to the following documents:

 * Critical updates for IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA appliances [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21390112] (for guidance when migration to a later firmware level)
- `E4.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 How do I add the Application Optimization feature to an IBM WebSphere DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance?
- `E4.S3`: The following document provides assistance on upgrading a DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance to add the Option for Application Optimization feature.
- `E4.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To add the Application Optimization feature:
- `E4.S5`: * The appliance must be a Type 9235 XML Security Gateway XS40 or Integration Appliance XI50 running firmware 3.7.3.0 or later or must be a Type 4195 Integration Blade XI50B running firmware 3.8.1.0 or later.
   Note: For Type 7199 appliances, see technote 1501194 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501194]. 
 * You purchased the feature and received a letter that contains the Controlled Access Key to download the firmware image.
- `E4.S6`: Part 1: Accessing the Web site that contains the firmware image. 
Using your IBM account and Controlled Access Key, access the web site to download the firmware image that contains the Application Optimization feature. 
 1. Identify the serial number for your appliance  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Version Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show version command.
- `E4.S7`: 2. Follow the instructions in the Authorized Feature Download letter to access the WebSphere DataPower Registered Downloads portal [http://www.ibm.com/services/forms/preLogin.do?lang=en_US&source=swg-datapowerapps]. 
 3. Sign in using your IBM user ID and password. Register, if you do not have an ID. 
 4. Enter the Controlled Access Key in the letter to access the web page containing the firmware images. Ensure that the first 7-characters of the Controlled Access Key in the letter matches the serial number for the appliance that you obtained in step 1.
- `E4.S8`: You are now ready to continue to Part 2 to download the firmware image.
- `E4.S9`: Part 2: Downloading the firmware image. 
Determine which firmware image you need and download that image.
- `E4.S10`: Notes:  * Starting with version 3.8.1, firmware that contain the MQ libraries do not contain .mq as part of its file name. 
 * If you purchased the Option for Application Optimization feature after 10-June-2011, there is only a single image. Therefore, you do not need to identify libraries to determine which image to download.
- `E4.S11`: 1. Identify the library information for your appliance. That is whether the appliance has the libraries for the Database connection (ODBC), IBM Tivoli Access Manager (TAM), WebSphere MQ (MQ), and TIBCO EMS features.  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Library Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show library-version command.
- `E4.S12`: 2. Download the image that corresponds to the available libraries on your appliance. For example:  * Download xs3800.tam6.scrypt2 if your XML Security Gateway XS40 has TAM 6.0 
     * Download xi3800.mq.odbc.tam61.scrypt2 if your Integration Appliance XI50 has ODBC, MQ, and TAM 6.1
- `E4.S13`: 3. Do not transfer the image to the appliance at this time. You will install the image in Part 4: Installing the firmware image.
- `E4.S14`: Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash.
- `E4.S15`: at this time. You will install the image in Part 4: Installing the firmware image.
- `E4.S16`: Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash. The steps in this flash provide additional information to use with the upgrade documentation in the information center. 
 2. Save the current configuration.  * From the WebGUI, click Save Config. 
     * From the command line, issue the write memory command.
- `E4.S17`: 3. Create a backup of the entire system, and store the configuration in a safe location off of the appliance. 
 4. Confirm that you have a working admin account and a back up privileged account that can change the password for the admin account, if needed. 
 5. Make sure that the passwords for both accounts were recently changed.
- `E4.S18`: Part 4: Installing the firmware image. 
Install the firmware image. Each firmware image uses the serial number of the appliance as the key. 
 1. Remove appliance from production. 
 2. Following the instructions upgrade documentation in the information center:  * Remove extraneous files 
     * Reboot the appliance to release temporary storage 
     * Transfer the firmware image to the appliance 
     * Install the firmware image
- `E4.S19`: 3. Verify that the appliance has the Application Optimization feature.  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Device Features. The list includes Option for Application Optimization. 
     * From the command line, issue the show features command. The list includes AppOpt.
- `E4.S20`: If the installation is successful and the list does not include the Application Optimization feature, the most likely reason is that the firmware image was for a different appliance. Each firmware image to add the Application Optimization feature uses the serial number of the appliance as the key. If you install a downloaded image to a different appliance, you will notice that the firmware is upgraded to that firmware level and that the Application for Optimization feature is not available.
- `E4.S21`: If you accessed the download site using the Controlled Access Key and installed the downloaded image to the appliance with the matching serial number and the feature list does not include the Application Optimization feature, contact IBM Support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322].
- `E4.S22`: Contacting IBM Support 
When reporting the problem to IBM Support, the representative will need your Controlled Access Key in addition to the standard information to include. Go to Contacting IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliances Support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322].

I need to understand details regarding "Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM Java Runtime affect IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker" This is related to
CVE-2017-10115
CVE-2017-10116
CVE-2017-10109
CVE-2017-10108

Where can I find this information?

Reference / gold answer:
You can find the details regarding the "Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM Java Runtime affect IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker" in the provided context under the section titled "IIB; WMB SECURITY BULLETIN." This section contains information about the vulnerabilities, including CVE IDs, descriptions, CVSS scores, affected products, remediation/fixes, and references.

- `E2.S1`: WMB IIB SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E2.S2`: SUMMARY
 Multiple security vulnerabilities exist in the IBM® Runtime Environment Java™ Technology Edition 6.0.16.26 (and earlier) used by WebSphere Message Broker, and the IBM® Runtime Environment Java™ Technology Edition 7.0.9.40 (and earlier) used by WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus, and the IBM® Runtime Environment Java™ Technology Edition 7.1.3.40 (and earlier) used by IBM Integration Bus. These issues were disclosed as part of the IBM Java SDK updates in July 2016.

Status: `ANSWER`

Visible answer:
The IBM security bulletin is available at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21697107. [E4.S3]

It covers multiple vulnerabilities in IBM SDK Java Technology Edition 7.1.4.10 and IBM Runtime Environment Java versions 7.0.10.10 and 7.1.4.10 used by IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker; the issues were disclosed in the July 2017 IBM Java SDK updates. [E1.S2]

CVE-2017-10115 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information; its CVSS base score is 7.5. [E1.S5]

CVE-2017-10116 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take control of the system; its CVSS base score is 8.3. [E1.S6]

CVE-2017-10108 and CVE-2017-10109 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service; each has a CVSS base score of 5.3. [E1.S7] [E1.S8]

The affected products include IBM Integration Bus V9.0.0.0–V9.0.0.8 and V10.0.0.0–V10.0.0.9, plus WebSphere Message Broker V7.0.0.0–V7.0.0.8 and V8.0.0.0–V8.0.0.9. [E1.S9] [E1.S10]

For remediation, APAR IT21764 is available in IBM Integration Bus fix packs 10.0.0.10 and 9.0.0.9; for WebSphere Message Broker V7 and V8, contact IBM Support to request the fix. [E1.S12]

For the complete list of IBM Java SDK vulnerabilities, consult the IBM Java SDK Security Bulletin in the References section: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21986642. [E1.S4] [E2.S12]

Visible answer:
The information is in IBM’s security bulletin for IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker. It covers multiple vulnerabilities in IBM SDK Java Technology Edition 7.1.4.10 and IBM Runtime Environment Java versions 7.0.10.10 and 7.1.4.10, disclosed in the July 2017 IBM Java SDK updates. [E1.S1]

For the complete vulnerability list, the bulletin refers to the “IBM Java SDK Security Bulletin” in its References section: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21986642 [E1.S1] [E4.S1]

The bulletin identifies CVE-2017-10115, CVE-2017-10116, CVE-2017-10108, and CVE-2017-10109. The affected products include IBM Integration Bus V9.0.0.0–V9.0.0.8 and V10.0.0.0–V10.0.0.9, and WebSphere Message Broker V7.0.0.0–V7.0.0.8 and V8.0.0.0–V8.0.0.9. [E1.S1]

The listed fixes are APAR IT21764: IBM Integration Bus V10 fix pack 10.0.0.10, IBM Integration Bus V9 fix pack 9.0.0.9, and IBM support assistance for WebSphere Message Broker V7 and V8. [E1.S1]

## techqa_DEV_Q220#row-0046

Question:
Help with Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System (CVE-2014-8730) I need to understand details regarding "Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System (CVE-2014-8730)". Where can I find this information? 

Reference / gold answer:
You can find detailed information about the "Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System (CVE-2014-8730)" in the provided context above. It includes a summary of the vulnerability, vulnerability details, affected products and versions, remediation/fixes, workarounds and mitigations, references, related information, acknowledgements, change history, and disclaimer.

Reference evidence:
- `2a`:  SECURITY BULLETIN SUMMARY
- `2b`:  Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects IBM PureApplication System. VULNERABILITY DETAILS

- `E3.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E3.S2`: SUMMARY
 Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects TPF Toolkit.
- `E3.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVE-ID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
- `E3.S4`: DESCRIPTION: Product could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations. A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plaintext of secure connections.
- `E3.S5`: CVSS Base Score: 4.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)
- `E3.S6`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
TPF Toolkit 3.6.x, 4.0.x, and 4.2.x
- `E3.S7`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
All current versions of TPF Toolkit ship JREs that are not impacted by this vulnerability. However, TPF Toolkit provides a Remote System Explorer (RSE) daemon that runs on Linux for System z. This daemon relies on the Java that is installed on that system. Ensure that the Java level currently installed on your Linux for System z system is up to date. The minimum level of Java that is required includes the fix for vulnerability CVE-2013-0169 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IV37656].
- `E3.S8`: WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
None

CVEID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
- `E4.S4`: DESCRIPTION: IBM Security Access Manager for DataPower could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations. A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plaintext of secure connections.
- `E4.S5`: CVSS Base Score: 4.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See http://xforce.iss.net/xforce/xfdb/99216 [http://xforce.iss.net/xforce/xfdb/99216] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)
- `E4.S6`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
IBM Security Access Manager version 8.0.0.5 for DataPower in all WebSphere DataPower Gateway appliances version 7.1.0.
- `E4.S7`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
None
- `E4.S8`: WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
The following steps describe how to mitigate this vulnerability for the affected releases. You should verify applying this configuration change does not cause any compatibility issues.
- `E4.S9`: Mitigation for IBM Security Access Manager for DataPower 8.0.0.5
- `E4.S10`: 1. Select Objects > Security Access Manager > Access Manager Reverse Proxy from the WebGUI navigation panel. 
 2. Select the Reverse Proxy instance. 
 3. Select the Manage Files tab and then the Edit button for the Configuration File property. 
 4. In the [ssl] stanza, add the bold lines below to the following two sections.
    # Specify any additional GSKit attributes which should be used when 
    # initializing an SSL connection with the client. A complete list of 
    # the available attributes is included in the GSKit SSL API
    # documentation.
    # 
    # The configuration entry may be specified multiple times, one for each 
    # GSKit attribute. The entry should be of the format: 
    # gsk-attr-name = <type>:<id>:<value> 
    # 
    # - where <type> is one of 'enum', 'string', 'number' 
    # and <id> corresponds to the identity associated with a GSKit attribute
    # (e.g., GSK_HTTP_PROXY_SERVER_NAME = 225) 
    # 
    # An example configuration could be: 
    # gsk-attr-name = string:225:proxy.ibm.com
- `E4.S11`: gsk-attr-name = enum:471:1
- `E4.S12`: # Specify any additional GSKit attributes which should be used when 
    # initializing an SSL connection with a junctioned server. A complete 
    # list of the available attributes is included in the GSKit SSL API 
    # documentation. 
    #
    # The configuration entry may be specified multiple times, one for each
    # GSKit attribute. The entry should be of the format: 
    # jct-gsk-attr-name = <type>:<id>:<value> 
    # 
    # - where <type> is one of 'enum', 'string', 'number' 
    # and <id> corresponds to the identity associated with a GSKit attribute
    # (e.g., GSK_HTTP_PROXY_SERVER_NAME = 225) 
    # 
    # An example configuration could be: 
    # jct-gsk-attr-name = string:225:proxy.ibm.com
- `E4.S13`: jct-gsk-attr-name = enum:471:1 
 5. Click Apply to deploy the changes.

- `E5.S1`: CVE-2014-8730 SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E5.S2`: SUMMARY
 Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects IBM Rational ClearCase.
- `E5.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVE-ID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
Description: IBM Rational ClearCase could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations. A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plaintext of secure connections.
- `E5.S4`: CVSS Base Score: 4.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)
- `E5.S5`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
CMI and OSLC integrations (Windows platform)
The vulnerable component is used when ClearCase on Windows platforms is configured to integrate with IBM Rational ClearQuest or Rational Team Concert with communication over SSL (https). This applies to Base CC/CQ integrations using Change Management Interface (CMI) and to UCM-enabled CQ integration via OSLC. The UCM-enabled CQ integration without using OSLC (SQUID) is not sensitive to this attack.
The integrations may be used by Windows clients directly, or by a Windows CCRC WAN server/CM Server.
- `E5.S6`: ClearCase Windows Client or CCRC WAN Server/CM Server Version Status 8.0.1.x Affected if you use CMI or OSLC integrations 8.0.0.5 and higher Affected if you use CMI or OSLC integrations 7.1.2.9 and higher Affected if you use CMI or OSLC integrations 7.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.1.1.x Not affected 
Note: Linux/UNIX clients using CMI or OSLC integrations are not affected. Linux/UNIX WAN servers are not affected by this vulnerability in CMI/OSLC, but are affected by a vulnerability in IBM HTTP Server (IHS). 
CCRC WAN Server (All platforms)
- `E5.S7`: The vulnerable component is also used by CCRC WAN server (all platforms) and CM Server for ClearCase (all platforms) when supporting SSL connections with IBM HTTP Server.
- `E5.S8`: ClearCase server version Status of IHS vulnerability 8.0.1.x (CCRC WAN server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 8.0.0.x (CCRC WAN server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 7.1.2.x (CM Server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 7.1.1.x (CM Server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 7.1.0.x (CM Server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL REMEDIATION/FIXES
Install the appropriate fix pack on your Windows systems running the vulnerable integration code (clients and servers):
- `E5.S9`: Affected Versions Applying the fix to Windows clients using an integration 8.0.1.x Install Rational ClearCase Fix Pack 7 (8.0.1.7) for 8.0.1 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24039409] 8.0.0.x Install Rational ClearCase Fix Pack 14 (8.0.0.14) for 8.0 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24039407] 7.1.2.x 
7.1.1.x 
7.1.0.x Customers on extended support contracts should install Rational ClearCase Fix Pack 17 (7.1.2.17) for 7.1.2 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24039405] You should verify applying this fix does not cause any compatibility issues.
- `E5.S10`: In addition to the above fix pack, you should install a fix for IBM HTTP server on your CCRC WAN server/CM Server host(s). Apply the fixes listed in Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM HTTP Server (CVE-2014-8730) [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21692502]. To install a fixpack or interim fix for IHS as referenced in that bulletin, follow the guidance in this table:
- `E5.S11`: Affected ClearCase Versions Applying an IHS Fix 8.0.0.x, 8.0.1.x Install the IHS fixes to your installation, following the instructions from the IHS security bulletin.

Status: `ANSWER`

Visible answer:
The security bulletin information is provided in IBM’s bulletin for IBM PureApplication System. It covers a TLS padding vulnerability exploited through a POODLE-like attack. [E1.S1] [E1.S2]

The vulnerability is CVE-2014-8730. IBM PureApplication Server bundles IBM HTTP Server, whose failure to check TLS CBC padding bytes could allow a man-in-the-middle attacker to decrypt sensitive information and calculate plaintext from secure connections. The CVSS base score is 4.3. [E1.S3]

Affected releases listed are IBM PureApplication System V1.1, V2.0, and V2.1. [E1.S4] [E1.S6]

For remediation, apply an update to the Web Application pattern type included with IBM PureApplication System. Fix Central links are provided for V2.1 and V2.0; the bulletin separately lists V1.1 and earlier. [E1.S7] [E1.S8] [E1.S9] [E1.S10] [E1.S11] [E1.S12]

You can find related IBM security information through the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal and the IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog. IBM also recommends subscribing to My Notifications for future security bulletins. [E1.S15] [E1.S17]

=== CANDIDATE B ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: CVE-2014-8730 SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E1.S2`: SUMMARY
 Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects IBM Rational ClearCase.
- `E1.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVE-ID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
Description: IBM Rational ClearCase could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations. A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plaintext of secure connections.
- `E1.S4`: CVSS Base Score: 4.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)
- `E1.S5`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
CMI and OSLC integrations (Windows platform)
The vulnerable component is used when ClearCase on Windows platforms is configured to integrate with IBM Rational ClearQuest or Rational Team Concert with communication over SSL (https). This applies to Base CC/CQ integrations using Change Management Interface (CMI) and to UCM-enabled CQ integration via OSLC. The UCM-enabled CQ integration without using OSLC (SQUID) is not sensitive to this attack.
The integrations may be used by Windows clients directly, or by a Windows CCRC WAN server/CM Server.
- `E1.S6`: ClearCase Windows Client or CCRC WAN Server/CM Server Version Status 8.0.1.x Affected if you use CMI or OSLC integrations 8.0.0.5 and higher Affected if you use CMI or OSLC integrations 7.1.2.9 and higher Affected if you use CMI or OSLC integrations 7.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.1.1.x Not affected 
Note: Linux/UNIX clients using CMI or OSLC integrations are not affected. Linux/UNIX WAN servers are not affected by this vulnerability in CMI/OSLC, but are affected by a vulnerability in IBM HTTP Server (IHS). 
CCRC WAN Server (All platforms)
- `E1.S7`: The vulnerable component is also used by CCRC WAN server (all platforms) and CM Server for ClearCase (all platforms) when supporting SSL connections with IBM HTTP Server.
- `E1.S8`: ClearCase server version Status of IHS vulnerability 8.0.1.x (CCRC WAN server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 8.0.0.x (CCRC WAN server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 7.1.2.x (CM Server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 7.1.1.x (CM Server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL 7.1.0.x (CM Server) Affected (all platforms) if you use SSL REMEDIATION/FIXES
Install the appropriate fix pack on your Windows systems running the vulnerable integration code (clients and servers):
- `E1.S9`: Affected Versions Applying the fix to Windows clients using an integration 8.0.1.x Install Rational ClearCase Fix Pack 7 (8.0.1.7) for 8.0.1 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24039409] 8.0.0.x Install Rational ClearCase Fix Pack 14 (8.0.0.14) for 8.0 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24039407] 7.1.2.x 
7.1.1.x 
7.1.0.x Customers on extended support contracts should install Rational ClearCase Fix Pack 17 (7.1.2.17) for 7.1.2 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24039405] You should verify applying this fix does not cause any compatibility issues.
- `E1.S10`: In addition to the above fix pack, you should install a fix for IBM HTTP server on your CCRC WAN server/CM Server host(s). Apply the fixes listed in Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM HTTP Server (CVE-2014-8730) [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21692502]. To install a fixpack or interim fix for IHS as referenced in that bulletin, follow the guidance in this table:
- `E1.S11`: Affected ClearCase Versions Applying an IHS Fix 8.0.0.x, 8.0.1.x Install the IHS fixes to your installation, following the instructions from the IHS security bulletin.

- `E2.S8`: WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
The following steps describe how to mitigate this vulnerability for the affected releases. You should verify applying this configuration change does not cause any compatibility issues.
- `E2.S9`: Mitigation for IBM Security Access Manager for DataPower 8.0.0.5
- `E2.S10`: 1. Select Objects > Security Access Manager > Access Manager Reverse Proxy from the WebGUI navigation panel. 
 2. Select the Reverse Proxy instance. 
 3. Select the Manage Files tab and then the Edit button for the Configuration File property. 
 4. In the [ssl] stanza, add the bold lines below to the following two sections.
    # Specify any additional GSKit attributes which should be used when 
    # initializing an SSL connection with the client. A complete list of 
    # the available attributes is included in the GSKit SSL API
    # documentation.
    # 
    # The configuration entry may be specified multiple times, one for each 
    # GSKit attribute. The entry should be of the format: 
    # gsk-attr-name = <type>:<id>:<value> 
    # 
    # - where <type> is one of 'enum', 'string', 'number' 
    # and <id> corresponds to the identity associated with a GSKit attribute
    # (e.g., GSK_HTTP_PROXY_SERVER_NAME = 225) 
    # 
    # An example configuration could be: 
    # gsk-attr-name = string:225:proxy.ibm.com
- `E2.S11`: gsk-attr-name = enum:471:1
- `E2.S12`: # Specify any additional GSKit attributes which should be used when 
    # initializing an SSL connection with a junctioned server. A complete 
    # list of the available attributes is included in the GSKit SSL API 
    # documentation. 
    #
    # The configuration entry may be specified multiple times, one for each
    # GSKit attribute. The entry should be of the format: 
    # jct-gsk-attr-name = <type>:<id>:<value> 
    # 
    # - where <type> is one of 'enum', 'string', 'number' 
    # and <id> corresponds to the identity associated with a GSKit attribute
    # (e.g., GSK_HTTP_PROXY_SERVER_NAME = 225) 
    # 
    # An example configuration could be: 
    # jct-gsk-attr-name = string:225:proxy.ibm.com
- `E2.S13`: jct-gsk-attr-name = enum:471:1 
 5. Click Apply to deploy the changes.

 Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects IBM PureApplication System.
- `E3.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
DESCRIPTION: IBM PureApplication Server bundles IBM HTTP Server, which could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations. A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plain text of secure connections.

- `E3.S5`: This vulnerability affects all versions and releases of IBM HTTP Server (powered by Apache) component in all editions of WebSphere Application Server and bundling products. IBM PureApplication Server bundles WebSphere Application Server in its Web Application Pattern.

## techqa_DEV_Q237#row-0031

Question:
Traffic across domains seems unexpected 

I have two Multi-Protocol Gateways (MPGWs) configured, each in their own domain:

     Domain A
     MPGW_A
     FSH_A (1.2.3.4:443)
     Domain B
     MPGW_B
     FSH_B (0.0.0.0:443)

The FSH_B is disabled, thus MPGW_B cannot take traffic. However, if I modify the config for MPGW_B (i.e. just change a Stylesheet parameter) the traffic goes to MPGW_B somehow. How is this happening? FSH_B is still disabled.

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the given context, the unexpected traffic across domains could be happening due to the configuration of cross-certification between the two domains. In the context provided, it mentions setting up cross-certification for user access and replication. 

If there is cross-certification set up between Domain A and Domain B for user access, it is possible that this cross-certification is allowing traffic to flow from Domain A to Domain B, even if the FSH_B is disabled in MPGW_B. 

To investigate further, you may need to review the cross-certification setup between the two domains and ensure that it is configured only for user access in one direction as intended. Additionally, checking the configuration of the MPGWs and the traffic routing rules within the domains may also provide insights into how the traffic is being redirected to MPGW_B despite FSH_B being disabled.

Reference evidence:


=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E2.S1`: datapower; routing; route; default; static; gateway; default gateway; static route TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The default route and static routes on the DataPower appliance have different functionality and behavior.
- `E2.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
A static route forces the DataPower appliance to use a specific interface and a specific set of network hops to access a given set of destinations. The "default route" is created by setting the Default Gateway of an interface on a DataPower appliance.
- `E2.S4`: A default route will be used if a known route does not exist for a given destination address. If multiple default routes are configured, the appliance will randomly pick which interface to use for outbound traffic if a more specific route cannot be found.
- `E2.S5`: If you want your network traffic to follow a specific route, set a static route and NOT rely on the default gateway. As a general rule, the management interface should not have the default gateway set, as you generally want to restrict the connections that can be made through that interface.
- `E2.S6`: A general recommendation is to set specific static routes and only ONE default gateway that will catch all traffic not being directed by the static routes.
- `E2.S7`: Consider the following example after running this command from the CLI:
- `E2.S8`: xs40# show route
- `E2.S9`: destination interface gateway metric 0.0.0.0/0 eth0 167.91.8.1 0 0.0.0.0/0 eth1 167.91.7.1 0 0.0.0.0/0 mgt0 10.238.77.1 0 10.238.77.0/24 mgt0 [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21249208&amp;aid=1] 0 167.81.18.0/23 eth0 [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21249208&amp;aid=1] 0 167.81.18.0/23 eth1 [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21249208&amp;aid=1] 0
- `E2.S10`: The output above shows that three default gateways were configured on eth0, eth1, and mgt0 which causes three "default" route to be generated (0.0.0.0/0). If the destination address of your service is 166.84.23.4, the device will randomly choose any one of the default routes as no specific route is configured. If, for example, the gateway picked is 10.238.77.1 and the gateway does not know how to route to the needed backend server ip address, this will cause unexpected connection failures. In the case of such failure, a reboot of the device will lead to a different route to be randomly picked, thus temporarily resolving until the next failure.
- `E2.S11`: Firmware 3.7.2 and later
- `E2.S12`: Instructions for setting the default gateway and for setting a static route can be found in the "Managing the appliance" section of the Administrators Guide. The command line commands are ip default-gateway and ip route respectively, and more information is available in the CLI Reference Guide.
- `E2.S13`: Firmware earlier than 3.7.2
- `E2.S14`: Instructions for setting the default gateway and static routes can be found in the "Ethernet Interface" appendix of the WebGUI Guide. The command line commands are ip default-gateway and ip route respectively, and more information is available in the CLI Reference Guide.

- `E4.S5`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  When a Gateway node is removed from an IBM API Management
   environment, there are some scenarios where the configuration
   of the Gateway node might not be successfully cleaned. If the
   administrator tries to add the same Gateway node back in to
   the environment, the following error is displayed.
- `E4.S6`: error message key:
   error message text: "An error ocurred while adding the gateway
   appliance ''${0}'' to the loadbalancer group used for internal
   traffic. The error was: ${1}: ${2}"
- `E4.S7`: LOCAL FIX
 *  This issue can be resolved by manually removing the load
   balancer configuration from the Gateway node (DataPower
   appliance). To manually remove the load balancer, run the
   following CLI or GUI commands:  (where your
   DataPower appliance is configured to use the network interface
   "eth0", and the load balancer group is "123")  By
   using the CLI:  * ssh <datapower hostname> *
   enter your login credentials * co * int eth0 * no
   standby 123 * exit * write mem  By using the
   DataPower user interface:  Open the Network and
   Interface folders in the navigation tree. * Click "Ethernet
   Interface". * Click the relevant interface row in the
   table. * Select the "Standby Control" tab. * Click X
   on the relevant table row to delete the load balancing
   group. * Click "Apply". * Click "Save Config" in the
   page header.  Also, to prevent any port conflicts,
   remove all IBM API Management domains from the Gateway node
   (DataPower appliance) too. The IBM API Management related
   domains have the format of "APIMgmt_<10 alphanumeric
   characters>". Otherwise, adding the Gateway node appears to
   complete successfully but when APIs that are created by using
   the recreated Management node are accessed, you see 404 errors.
- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  When a Gateway node is removed from an IBM API Management
   environment, there are some scenarios where the configuration of
   the Gateway node might not be successfully cleaned. If the

- `E4.S9`: In particular, this occurs if the Management node(s) of the

- `E5.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Affected are customers sending HTTP GET requests to the
   multiprotocol gateway, web service proxy or web application
   firewall service.
- `E5.S5`: With the present implementation, users may end up in a state
   with indefinite retries for HTTP GET requests as long as
   DataPower has at least one live persistent connection to the
   backend server. After timeout interval for active connection it
   will terminate the connection and retry using remaining
   persistent connections to the backend. (If a new connection is
   opened because of half-dead backend this can continue
   indefinitely or until the request is served).
- `E5.S6`: LOCAL FIX
 *  This behavior cannot be turned off however it can be mitigated.
   For some relief out of this, the admin can lower the Back
   Persistent Timeout and/or User Agent's default Timeout. This
   should result in less persistent connections to the backend and
   thus less possible timeout hops
- `E5.S7`: Dropping the backend persistent connections option is also a
   possible workaround, but the consequences should be weighed
   carefully before making this decision. Not using persistent
   connections comes with a performance penalty, but it very much
   depends on the size/type of the transferred data and the
   speed/ping of the network.
- `E5.S8`: SLM is also strongly encouraged to prevent the backend from
   getting more load than it can handle.
- `E5.S9`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  Affected are all customers using the Multi-Protocol Gateway,
   Web Service Proxy or Web Application Firewall with persistent
   connection to the backend side.
- `E5.S10`: In case the backend server stops responding to HTTP GET
   requests while there are already some established TCP
   connections from the time the server worked OK, DataPower will
   automatically retry those GET requests after a timeout period.
   This will be retried until there are no established connections
   to the server.
- `E5.S11`: During a high load window, these unwanted retries might
   eventually keep flooding an already congested backend,
   especially if it is still able to establish some new
   connections.
- `E5.S12`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Fix is available in 6.0.0.16, 6.0.1.12, 7.0.0.9, 7.1.0.6 and
   7.2.0.2.
- `E5.S13`: For a list of the latest fix packs available, please see:
   http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631]

- `E2.S1`: datapower; routing; route; default; static; gateway; default gateway; static route TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The default route and static routes on the DataPower appliance have different functionality and behavior.
- `E2.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
A static route forces the DataPower appliance to use a specific interface and a specific set of network hops to access a given set of destinations. The "default route" is created by setting the Default Gateway of an interface on a DataPower appliance.
- `E2.S4`: A default route will be used if a known route does not exist for a given destination address. If multiple default routes are configured, the appliance will randomly pick which interface to use for outbound traffic if a more specific route cannot be found.
- `E2.S5`: If you want your network traffic to follow a specific route, set a static route and NOT rely on the default gateway. As a general rule, the management interface should not have the default gateway set, as you generally want to restrict the connections that can be made through that interface.
- `E2.S6`: A general recommendation is to set specific static routes and only ONE default gateway that will catch all traffic not being directed by the static routes.
- `E2.S7`: Consider the following example after running this command from the CLI:
- `E2.S8`: xs40# show route
- `E2.S9`: destination interface gateway metric 0.0.0.0/0 eth0 167.91.8.1 0 0.0.0.0/0 eth1 167.91.7.1 0 0.0.0.0/0 mgt0 10.238.77.1 0 10.238.77.0/24 mgt0 [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21249208&amp;aid=1] 0 167.81.18.0/23 eth0 [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21249208&amp;aid=1] 0 167.81.18.0/23 eth1 [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21249208&amp;aid=1] 0
- `E2.S10`: The output above shows that three default gateways were configured on eth0, eth1, and mgt0 which causes three "default" route to be generated (0.0.0.0/0). If the destination address of your service is 166.84.23.4, the device will randomly choose any one of the default routes as no specific route is configured. If, for example, the gateway picked is 10.238.77.1 and the gateway does not know how to route to the needed backend server ip address, this will cause unexpected connection failures. In the case of such failure, a reboot of the device will lead to a different route to be randomly picked, thus temporarily resolving until the next failure.
- `E2.S11`: Firmware 3.7.2 and later
- `E2.S12`: Instructions for setting the default gateway and for setting a static route can be found in the "Managing the appliance" section of the Administrators Guide. The command line commands are ip default-gateway and ip route respectively, and more information is available in the CLI Reference Guide.
- `E2.S13`: Firmware earlier than 3.7.2
- `E2.S14`: Instructions for setting the default gateway and static routes can be found in the "Ethernet Interface" appendix of the WebGUI Guide. The command line commands are ip default-gateway and ip route respectively, and more information is available in the CLI Reference Guide.

## techqa_DEV_Q111#row-0130

Question:
StaleConnectionException errors with BPM databases There is much published documentation about stale connections to databases on the web, and yet stale connections continue to be a very common problem, at least with BPM databases. The condition can manifest itself in different ways. The most common experience of a stale connection is from error messages in the log or FFDCs that contain "StaleConnectionException".

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, the issue of StaleConnectionException errors with BPM databases may be caused by a problem with the JCC driver version. To resolve this issue, it is recommended to upgrade the JCC driver to version 3.59.81 that was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later, as this fix incorporates a solution for the stale connection exceptions. Additionally, as a workaround, "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" can be added to the definition of stored procedures on the host. It is also suggested to check for restrictions on using this clause and ensure that the APAR IZ07301 fix is applied. If the issue persists, contacting Technical Support for additional troubleshooting options may be necessary.

Reference evidence:
- `0b`: Websphere Application aborts after calling z/OS stored procedure because of stale connection exceptions. SYMPTOM
- `0c`: StaleConnectionException may be seen after upgrade JCC driver.
- `0j`: point, 0x2413 does not match expected code point, 0x2408. ERRORCODE=-
- `0k`: 4499, SQLSTATE=null:com.ibm.db2.jcc.am.qo: [jcc][t4][2028][11149]
- `0l`: [3.58.136] Actual code point, 0x2413 does not match expected code point, 0x2408. ERRORCODE=-4499, SQLSTATE=null
- `0n`: Fix for this issue incorporated in JCC driver version 3.59.81 that was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later (defect 134363): https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC66739 [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC66739]
- `0o`: As a workaround, "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" can be added to the definition of stored procedure on the host.
- `0p`: You might receive SQL0751N or XAER_NOTA on XA END while using "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" if stored procedure call is a part of XA transaction.
- `0q`: Please check for restriction on using this clause in the technote 1433093: https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433093 [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433093] or

- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 JRules and ODM modules such as Rule Execution Server (RES) and Rule Team Server (RTS) / Decision Center (DC) may fail to access their data source with the following type of exception present in the log:
- `E1.S3`: com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException: Io exception: Connection timed out
- `E1.S4`: SYMPTOM
The problem may occur when a JRules or ODM module accesses its data source after a period of database access inactivity. For example:
- `E1.S5`: * The first user accessing a RTS / DC server that remained idle overnight experiences a failure upon logging and the server log shows an com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException occurred at that time. 
 * After a RES server has been processing execution requests normally for some time, an attempt to deploy a ruleset update fails and the server log shows an com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException occurred upon an attempt to invalidate a ruleset or to retrieve its definition.
- `E1.S6`: CAUSE
The underlying network connection for a data source is no longer valid although the data source itself remains considered active from the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool management perspective. An attempt by a JRules module to try and access its data base through one such data source connection provided by the Application Server may then fail. 
The network connection of a data source may become invalid for a number of reasons, one typical example is that a firewall between the Application Server and the Database has a policy to discard network connections that remain idle for some time.
- `E1.S7`: ENVIRONMENT
The exception com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException is specific to WebSphere Application Server environments. But a similar issue can be experienced with Weblogic, see: Rule Execution Server on WebLogic unable to load ruleset after period of inactivity [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21615801]
- `E1.S8`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/v7r0/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/info/ae/ae/udat_conpoolset.html] so as to eliminate occurrences of StaleConnectionException :
- `E1.S9`: * Set the Minimum connections to 0 to avoid situations where a connection is kept in the pool to meet the minimum requirement, even though it may have been idle for longer than Unused timeout 
 * Set the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that the sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout
- `E1.S10`: The document Troubleshooting stale connection problems [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21247168#SCETroubleshooting] provides further information. RELATED INFORMATION
#RES unable to load ruleset after period of inactivity [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21615801]
Troubleshooting stale connection problems [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21247168#SCETroubleshooting]
- `E1.S11`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration IBM Operational Decision Manager Platform Independent 8.5, 8.0.1, 8.0, 7.5 Enterprise
- `E2.S1`: stale connection; unable to access database TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM
Stale connections can occur after Portal server has been idle for a period of time and attempts to access the database.
- `E2.S3`: [1/19/12 22:16:42:351 EST] 00000036 SchedulerDaem E SCHD0104E: The
Scheduler poll daemon WPSTaskScheduler (wps/Scheduler) failed to load
tasks from the database due to an exception: com.ibm.websphere.
scheduler.SchedulerNotAvailableException: com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.
StaleConnectionException: IO Error: A remote host did not respond
within the timeout period.
- `E2.S4`: SYMPTOM
After a period of inactivity, the Portal server becomes unresponsive.
- `E2.S5`: CAUSE
The Portal connection to the database is closed externally by a firewall or by the remote database due to inactivity. Because Portal is still holding onto this connection, we still think the connection is available, and so receive the stale connection exception.
- `E2.S6`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Reviewing the Portal's systemOut.log we see the stale connection exception when attempting to access the database.
- `E2.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The solution is to reduce the Minimum Connections to 0 on the data source.
- `E2.S8`: This will cause WAS to remove all connections after a period of inactivity.
- `E2.S9`: In the WAS admin console, go to Resources -> JDBC -> Data sources
- `E2.S10`: For each of the 6 db domains, select the Connection pools link and
edit the Minimum connection folder.
- `E2.S11`: Restart the servers after the changes are made.

Fix for this issue incorporated in JCC driver version 3.59.81 that was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later (defect 134363):
https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC66739 [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC66739]

- `E3.S9`: You might receive SQL0751N or XAER_NOTA on XA END while using "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" if stored procedure call is a part of XA transaction. 
Please check for restriction on using this clause in the technote 1433093: https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433093 [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433093] 
or

- `E4.S1`: ETL job; JTS; common job; AbstractActivationManagerOwner; IllegalStateException; datawarehouse; database migration; service proxy; stale service TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Attempts to run an IBM Rational Jazz Team Server (JTS) "Common" job fails with an error "java.lang.IllegalStateException: This service proxy does not have a reference to the most current instance in the service manager".
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
Steps to reproduce:
- `E4.S4`: 1. Migrate data warehouse to a different database, for example, from Derby to IBM DB2
- `E4.S5`: 2. Run the JTS Common job using the WebUI:
- `E4.S6`: https://[your-server-name]:[port]/jts/admin#action=com.ibm.team.reportsManagement.etlConfig
- `E4.S7`: The job fails and the following error message appears in the JTS log file:
- `E4.S8`: WARN internal.registry.AbstractActivationManagerOwner - An error occurred while trying to execute a service method java.lang.IllegalStateException: This service proxy does not have a reference to the most current instance in the service manager. If you hit this problem, your code is most likely holding onto a stale service reference and using it after it has been deactivated.
- `E4.S9`: CAUSE
The root cause of this problem is the change in the database settings for data warehouse connection.
- `E4.S10`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
SOLUTION
- `E4.S11`: Restart the JTS server to prevent the errors.

- `E5.S11`: Problem Description:
    a remote TEMS attached via ephemeral pipe will
   leave "stale" GLB entries (of the form "0.0.0.n")
   at the HUB if the remote TEMS re-registers without
   an intervening normal shutdown (where it explicitly
   unregisters the problem entries).  Once this occurs, the
   HUB will find the stale entries first, and cause distributed
   requests to that REMOTE to fail with connection errors even
   though the remote and any attached agents appear online.
- `E5.S12`: Detailed Recreation Procedure:
   Connect a remote TEMS to a HUB using the ephemeral keyword
   (KDE_TRANSPORT=...IP.PIPE EPHEMERAL:Y ...) in the configuration
   of the remote TEMS.  Once the remote TEMS has connected to the
   HUB and registered with the GLB, force a situation distribution
   to that remote TEMS.  Having then a situation distributed to the
   remote TEMS, crash that remote TEMS and restart it.  Once
   restarted, the HUB will experience comm failures trying to
   again distribute a situation to that remote TEMS.  The comm
   errors will be associated with the old remote TEMS address.
- `E5.S13`: Related Files and Output:
   The RAS1 log for the HUB will show communication failures to the
   remote TEMS with an address with an ephemeral address (of the
   form "0.0.0.n") which is not the address registered by that
   remote:
- `E5.S14`: KDSRU001   Remote request communication failure to destination
              *HUB ip.pipe:0.0.0.1.1918..
- `E5.S15`: Approver:
   nic
   *===============================================================
   ==
- `E5.S16`: Action Planned: Proceed with defect resolution.
- `E5.S17`: LOCAL FIX
 *  n/a
- `E5.S18`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All ITMS/ENGINE users.                       *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: STALE EPHEMERAL LB ENTRIES LEAD TO      *
   *                      CONNECTION ERRORS                       *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: Apply the PTF.                               *
   ****************************************************************
   A remote TEMS attached via ephemeral pipe will leave "stale"
   GLB entries (of the form "0.0.0.n") at the HUB if the remote
   TEMS re-registers without an intervening normal shutdown
   (where it explicitly unregisters the problem entries). This
   typically occurs when a remote TEMS crashes after connecting
   to the HUB. Once this crash happens, the HUB will find old,
   stale remote TEMS entries first, and cause distributed
   requests to that REMOTE to fail with connection errors even
   though the remote and any attached agents appear online.
- `E5.S19`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Code in Basic Services was changed to remove all ephemeral
   addresses on behalf of the remote TEMS when NETWORK and
   INTERFACE compare flags are set on the same call. Code in the
   TEMS was changed to (re)register the remote TEMS address with
   each heartbeat, thus maintaining currency.
- `E5.S20`: TEMPORARY FIX

Status: `ANSWER`

Visible answer:
A stale connection occurs when the underlying network connection to the database is no longer valid, while WebSphere Application Server still considers the pooled data-source connection active. A firewall or remote database may discard connections that remain idle, causing the subsequent database access to fail with StaleConnectionException. [E1.S6] [E2.S5]

The problem commonly appears after a period of database inactivity—for example, when the first user accesses an RTS/Decision Center server after it was idle overnight, or when a Portal server attempts to access its database after inactivity. [E1.S4] [E1.S5] [E2.S2] [E2.S4]

For WebSphere Application Server, set the data-source connection pool Minimum connections to 0. This prevents connections from being retained solely to satisfy a minimum-pool requirement and causes WAS to remove connections after inactivity. [E1.S8] [E1.S9] [E2.S7] [E2.S8]

Configure Unused timeout and Reap timeout so their sum does not exceed any network-level idle connection timeout. [E1.S9]

In the WAS administrative console, navigate to Resources → JDBC → Data sources, edit the Connection pools settings for each applicable data source, and restart the servers after making the changes. [E2.S9] [E2.S10] [E2.S11]
